title: Auditable Federated Learning for Multimodal Brain Tumor Classification under Label Skew and Client Dropout
abstract: Abstract Federated learning (FL) allows hospitals to collaboratively train deep learning models without exchanging patient images, but reported FL studies in medical imaging often assume independent and identically distributed (IID) client data and full participation in every communication round both conditions seldom hold in real clinical networks. Furthermore, although the entire premise of FL rests on the iterative averaging of client weight updates, the optimisation dynamics of those weights are rarely audited at the round level, limiting clinicians' and regulators' ability to inspect how the global model evolves under stress. This study presents an auditable federated framework for binary brain-tumour classification from a combined multimodal dataset of 4618 axial computed-tomography (CT) and 5000 magnetic-resonance imaging (MRI) slices, totalling 9618 labelled images. A lightweight three-block convolutional neural network is trained across five simulated clients using FedProx with proximal coefficient µ = 0.01 and FedAvg aggregation, under two contrasting client partitions: an IID scenario in which each client receives a balanced sample of healthy and tumour cases, and a deliberately aggressive non-IID scenario in which each client is assigned an 80% majority class. Clinically realistic stress is added by dropping a randomly chosen client in approximately 30% of rounds. At every round, for every active client, the framework records three weight summaries initial (received from the server), updated (after local training), and aggregated (new global model) together with per-client accuracy, loss, precision, recall, F1-score, communication payload, wall-clock round time, and process memory. After ten communication rounds, the global model attains 96.05% accuracy and an F1-score of 0.9641 on the held-out test set under the IID partition, and 94.96% accuracy with F1 0.9547 under the 80% label-skew non-IID partition, corresponding to an IID-to-non-IID degradation of only 1.09 percentage points despite the severe class skew and 30% per-round client dropout. Inspection of the weight-audit trace reveals a consistent and measurable shift in the output-layer mean under non-IID training that is invisible in conventional accuracy curves, suggesting that round-level weight auditing can serve as a lightweight forensic signal of distributional drift in federated medical AI.

title: MRI-Based Radiomics and Machine Learning for Predicting Refractory Outcomes in Ménière’s Disease: A Multicenter Preliminary Study
abstract: Abstract Objective To evaluate the value of a machine learning model based on radiomics features derived from multicenter gadolinium-enhanced inner ear magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) for predicting refractory clinical outcomes in patients with Ménière’s disease (MD). Methods This retrospective study enrolled patients with unilateral Ménière’s disease diagnosed at two medical centers between January 2019 and December 2023. A total of 154 patients from Center 1 constituted the internal dataset and were divided into a training set (n = 123) and an internal test set (n = 31) at an 8:2 ratio, while 32 patients from Center 2 were included as an independent external validation set. According to established clinical guidelines, patients were categorized into good-control and poor-control groups. Radiomics features were extracted from the cochlea and vestibule on gadolinium-enhanced 3D-FLAIR-CUBE images, and bilateral difference (Diff) features were generated by subtracting contralateral ear features from those of the affected ear. Feature selection was performed using correlation filtering and least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) regression. Multiple machine learning algorithms were used to construct predictive models, which were evaluated in both internal and external datasets. Model performance was assessed using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, and F1 score, and clinical utility was evaluated using decision curve analysis (DCA). Results In both the training and internal test sets, the Diff radiomics model achieved higher AUCs than the symptomatic-ear radiomics models (training set: 0.815 vs. 0.682; internal test set: 0.730 vs. 0.650), along with improved sensitivity and F1 scores. Feature importance analysis indicated that vestibular-related radiomics features contributed more prominently to the prediction of refractory outcomes. Although model performance declined in the external validation set, the Diff model maintained high sensitivity (0.957) and F1 score. DCA demonstrated greater clinical net benefit of the Diff model in the training and internal test sets. Conclusion A machine learning model based on bilateral difference radiomics features can effectively predict refractory outcomes in MD and demonstrates superior performance compared with single-ear radiomics models. This approach may provide objective imaging support for prognostic assessment and individualized management of patients with MD.

title: Unintentional Weight Loss Preceding Relapsing-Remitting Multiple Sclerosis: A Case Report and Review of Possible Mechanisms
abstract: Abstract Background Unintentional weight loss is not a recognized presenting feature of multiple sclerosis (MS) and is more commonly associated with malignancy, chronic infection, endocrine disorders, gastrointestinal disease, or systemic inflammatory conditions. We report an unusual case in which marked involuntary weight loss preceded the diagnosis of relapsing-remitting multiple sclerosis (RRMS). Case Presentation: A 37-year-old man presented with acute gait impairment and right lower-extremity weakness. Retrospective history revealed gradual unintentional weight loss from approximately 97 kg to 68 kg over nearly two years despite preserved appetite and the absence of gastrointestinal, infectious, endocrine, or constitutional symptoms. Extensive investigations, including laboratory testing, infectious screening, tumor markers, upper gastrointestinal endoscopy, abdominal ultrasonography, and chest imaging, failed to identify an alternative cause. Neurological examination demonstrated right lower-extremity weakness, generalized hyperreflexia, bilateral pyramidal signs, and an Expanded Disability Status Scale (EDSS) score of 4.0. Brain and cervical spinal cord magnetic resonance imaging revealed multiple typical demyelinating lesions fulfilling the 2017 McDonald criteria for MS. The patient received intravenous methylprednisolone followed by rituximab (1000 mg every 6 months). During four years of follow-up, the EDSS score improved from 4.0 to 1.0, MRI studies remained stable, and body weight gradually returned to two years before the start of the disease. Conclusion This case describes marked, unexplained weight loss preceding the diagnosis of RRMS, which resolved after treatment initiation and disease stabilization. Although causality cannot be established, the temporal association suggests that clinically significant weight loss may represent an uncommon and underrecognized manifestation of active MS. Further studies are needed to clarify the frequency and mechanisms of weight changes in MS.

title: Transcutaneous Skin Perforation by a Protruding Xiphoid Process in a Bedbound Patient With Post-Traumatic Cervical Myelopathy: A Case Report and Review of the Literature
abstract: Abstract Background The xiphoid process is the smallest and most morphologically variable component of the sternum, and anterior (ventral) deviation is a recognized anatomical variant. Symptomatic xiphoid disease typically presents as localized pain (xiphodynia). Cutaneous complications are exceedingly uncommon, and only a single previous report describing an ischemic xiphisternal ulcer associated with a protruding xiphoid has been published. To the best of our knowledge, we identified no previous English-language report describing complete transcutaneous perforation of the skin by a protruding xiphoid process associated with chronic sinus formation and secondary infection. Case presentation A 71-year-old bedbound man with type 2 diabetes mellitus, hypertension, and post-traumatic cervical myelopathy with spastic weakness developed progressive protrusion of the xiphoid process. The angulated xiphoid tip gradually eroded through the overlying skin, producing a chronic midline ulcer with sinus tract formation and superimposed infection. Lateral radiography demonstrated marked anterior angulation of the xiphoid process with prominent ventral protrusion and irregularity of the distal tip. The patient underwent xiphoidectomy with en-bloc excision of the ulcer and debridement of devitalized soft tissue. Intraoperative culture of the resected xiphoid specimen yielded extended-spectrum beta-lactamase (ESBL)-producing Escherichia coli, and culture-directed carbapenem therapy was administered. Histopathological examination revealed extensive ulceration with inflamed granulation tissue and a sinus tract, accompanied by reactive squamous epithelial hyperplasia (pseudoepitheliomatous hyperplasia), whereas the underlying bone was unremarkable and showed no evidence of malignancy. Conclusions A protruding xiphoid process can rarely progress beyond pain and superficial ulceration to cutaneous breach with sinus tract formation and secondary infection, particularly in debilitated patients with chronic immobility, diabetes mellitus, and reduced soft-tissue padding. This process appears mechanistically analogous to a pressure ulcer developing over an atypical bony prominence. Xiphoidectomy combined with debridement and culture-directed antimicrobial therapy appears to provide definitive treatment. Histopathological examination is essential because reactive pseudoepitheliomatous hyperplasia at the ulcer margin may mimic cutaneous malignancy.

title: Enhancing Structural Quality in Medical X-ray Super-Resolution via Domain-Aware Loss
abstract: Abstract Upscaling medical X-ray images is more challenging than enhancing natural images, because preserving accurate structural and boundary information is more important for diagnostic correctness than producing a realistic appearance. Super-resolution methods such as SRGAN, ESRGAN, and the Hybrid Attention Transformer (HAT) perform well on natural images, but when applied to medical images they can cause texture hallucination, obscure anatomical boundaries, and remove clinically important features. This study presents a comprehensive comparison of four approaches: standard SRGAN, standard ESRGAN with VGG-based perceptual loss, HAT with L1 loss, and the proposed optimised models ESRGAN_USELoss and HAT_USELoss, which incorporate a domain-specific loss function designed for X-ray imaging. The proposed USELoss (U-Net, Sobel and Edge Loss) replaces the computationally heavy VGG19 perceptual loss with a lightweight U-Net encoder that preserves multi-scale anatomical structures, and adds a Sobel-based edge loss to improve boundary accuracy, prioritising diagnostic fidelity over perceptual sharpness. On the PadChest X-ray dataset the quantitative results show large gains: standard ESRGAN reaches only 22.21 dB PSNR, whereas ESRGAN_USELoss reaches 34.04 dB, while HAT_USELoss achieves the best SSIM (0.9215) and LPIPS (0.1607). The proposed methods improve edge-preservation metrics by 5.5%, demonstrating that domain-specific loss functions are effective for clinically reliable medical image super-resolution. https://github.com/1aryantyagi/Segmentation-Paper is the Github repository of the code.

On the PadChest X-ray dataset the quantitative results show large gains: standard ESRGAN reaches only 22.21 dB PSNR, whereas ESRGAN_USELoss reaches 34.04 dB, while HAT_USELoss achieves the best SSIM (0.9215) and LPIPS (0.1607). The proposed methods improve edge-preservation metrics by 5.5%, demonstrating that domain-specific loss functions are effective for clinically reliable medical image super-resolution. https://github.com/1aryantyagi/Segmentation-Paper is the Github repository of the code.

title: Double filtration plasmapheresis in anti-amphiphysin antibody syndrome mimicking multiple system atrophy: A case report
abstract: Abstract We retrospectively analyzed a patient with a positive anti-amphiphysin antibody status to characterize the clinical manifestations, diagnostic workup, and treatment results of anti-amphiphysin antibody disease that mimics multiple system atrophy (MSA), and we reviewed the relevant literature. The patient primarily presented with Parkinsonism, cerebellar ataxia, and autonomic dysfunction. An 82-year-old male presented with a subacute onset of bradykinesia, ataxia, and severe orthostatic hypotension. Brain magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) revealed hippocampal and cerebellar atrophy. Serum autoimmune neurological antibody testing was positive for anti-amphiphysin IgG (titer 1:320). Based on the multisystem involvement and exclusionary diagnostic workup, the patient was diagnosed with anti-amphiphysin antibody-associated MSA-like autoimmune neurological syndrome. After three sessions of double filtration plasmapheresis (DFPP) and sequential therapy with mycophenolate mofetil, the patient's motor function and orthostatic hypotension improved significantly. At the 6-month follow-up, the antibody titer decreased to 1:32, and the clinical condition remained stable. Anti-amphiphysin antibody syndrome can mimic MSA. Prompt neuronal autoantibody and long-term tumor screening are required for rapidly progressive atypical MSA-spectrum patients with severe autonomic failure. DFPP combined with immunosuppression achieves a favorable neurological prognosis.

title: Cephalothoracoomphalopagus Tetrabrachius Tetrapus Conjoined Twins: An Extremely Rare Case Report
abstract: Abstract Background Conjoined twins are a rare subset of monozygotic twins that usually have a poor prognosis, which has become a significant cause of perinatal morbidity and mortality. This case highlights the importance of routine antenatal care for earlier prenatal diagnosis and well-informed family counseling concerning appropriate intervention for conjoined twins. Case presentation: A 31-year-old G2P1 female in 29 4/7 weeks of gestation was referred from a primary health care center to our hospital with conjoined twins. Two-dimensional (2D) and three-dimensional (3D) ultrasonography examinations at 29 4/7 weeks of gestation revealed one fetal head accompanied by an orbital hypotelorism with an interocular diameter of 0.99 cm. The liver and heart were found to be the fusion organs involved. Polyhydramnios was observed with a maximum vertical pocket of 12.07 cm. Diagnosis of cephalo-thoraco-omphalopagus conjoined twins was made right after the first scan and consistently confirmed thereafter by six more repeated ultrasound examinations. Clinical examination after scheduled surgical delivery in 33 5/7 weeks old neonates revealed male conjoined twins with a fused head accompanied by two pairs of ears, along with a single trunk together with four neurologically independent upper limbs and lower limbs, as well as two complements of genitalia and two anuses. The twin showed signs of respiratory distress and died within one hour of birth. Conclusion Routine antenatal care and advanced ultrasound scanning are crucial for earlier prenatal diagnosis and well-informed family counseling concerning appropriate intervention for conjoined twins.

title: A novel sub-junctional pinhole technique (S-PHT) in treating intrabony defects of stage III periodontitis – Case Series
abstract: Abstract Background Sub-junctional pinhole technique (S-PHT) is a minimally invasive approach in which graft material is introduced into the intrabony defect through a pinhole made on the facial surface opposite to the intrabony defect alveolar crest and apical to the junctional epithelium 4 weeks following minimally invasive non-surgical therapy. This strategy is intended to keep the long junctional epithelium as a biologic seal over the grafted material, while providing maximum soft tissue support around the grafted material. Methods This case series presents the short-term outcome of ten patients diagnosed with stage III grade A periodontitis with interproximal intrabony defects of at least 3 mm, treated with S-PHT. Xenogenic graft material was introduced into the defect through a facial pinhole opposite to the alveolar crest following defect degranulation using minimally invasive hand and ultrasonic instrumentation. Clinical and radiographic parameters were recorded at baseline (4 weeks after non-surgical therapy) and at 9 months following S-PHT. Results Nine months following S-PHT, all sites measured ≤ 4mm probing pocket depth (PPD). The number of sites with clinical attachment level (CAL) gain ≥ 3mm was 6 out of the 10 reported cases. Six sites out of the 10 cases fulfilled a composite outcome of pocket closure of ≤ 4 mm with ≥ 3 mm attachment gain and no bleeding on probing. Significant improvement in intrabony defect fill reported after 9 months with a mean defect fill of 3.1 mm (< 0.001). Conclusions This case series demonstrates that S-PHT, as a minimally invasive approach, could be a reliable patient friendly option for treating intrabony defects in stage III periodontitis. Trial Registration: ClinicalTrials.gov. identifiers NCT07763223 PRT-RCT-2026-001 (05-08-2026 and retrospectively registered 19-08-2026)

title: A Decade-Old Retained Intrapleural Glass Fragment in an Asymptomatic Skydiver: A Case Report and Review of the Literature
abstract: Abstract Retained intrathoracic foreign bodies are usually discovered after a traumatic event that the patient clearly remembers. Glass, however, can be especially problematic. It is frequently retained, may be missed during the initial assessment, can appear variably on imaging, and may migrate months or even years after injury rather than becoming securely encapsulated. To our knowledge, an entirely asymptomatic intrapleural glass fragment discovered incidentally in a skydiver has not previously been reported. We describe a 34-year-old male skydiver who was referred after a routine screening chest radiograph showed an abnormal shadow in the right hemithorax. Ten years earlier, he had sustained a penetrating right-sided chest injury during a parachute landing, when he crashed through a window. At that time, he was treated for haemopneumothorax with intercostal drainage, but no foreign body was suspected or actively sought. On current examination, he had a contracted right hemithorax. Computed tomography revealed a radio-dense pleural foreign body. Right-sided thoracotomy was performed, and a 7 × 2.5 cm glass fragment was removed from dense pleural adhesions. His postoperative recovery was uneventful, and he later returned to skydiving.

title: Follicular Dendritic Cell Sarcoma Arising in the Aortopulmonary Window: A Case Report of Complete Resection Using Proximal Pulmonary Artery Control
abstract: Abstract Background: Follicular dendritic cell sarcoma is a rare malignant neoplasm, and its occurrence in the aortopulmonary window is exceptionally uncommon. Tumors in this location are technically challenging because of the limited operative space and their close relationship to the aortic arch, left pulmonary artery, left main bronchus, and left recurrent laryngeal nerve. We report a case of follicular dendritic cell sarcoma arising in the aortopulmonary window that was completely resected using a strategy for proximal pulmonary artery control. Case presentation: A 46-year-old man was referred to our institution after an abnormal mediastinal shadow was incidentally detected on chest radiography. Contrast-enhanced computed tomography showed a 48 × 29 mm well-circumscribed mass in the aortopulmonary window, broadly contacting the aorta, left pulmonary artery, and left main bronchus. Positron emission tomography showed moderate fluorodeoxyglucose uptake without distant metastasis. Endobronchial ultrasound-guided transbronchial needle aspiration suggested a neuroendocrine tumor but did not establish a definitive diagnosis. Surgical resection was performed through median sternotomy combined with a left anterior second intercostal thoracotomy. Because direct exposure and encirclement of the tumor-adjacent left pulmonary artery were considered hazardous, proximal vascular control was established through the transverse pericardial sinus before tumor manipulation. Division of the ligamentum arteriosum increased pulmonary artery mobility and improved exposure of the operative field. The tumor was completely separated from the left pulmonary artery, aorta, left main bronchus, and recurrent laryngeal nerve without combined organ resection. Histopathological examination showed spindle-shaped tumor cells arranged in whorled and rosette-like patterns. Immunohistochemical staining was positive for CD21, CD23, D2-40, and somatostatin receptor 2, confirming follicular dendritic cell sarcoma. The postoperative course was uneventful, and the patient remained free of recurrence 3 years after surgery. Conclusions: Complete resection of a tumor arising in the aortopulmonary window can be facilitated by secure proximal pulmonary artery control and mobilization of surrounding structures. These technical principles may also be useful for other tumors in this anatomically complex region when direct manipulation of the tumor-adjacent pulmonary artery is considered hazardous.

title: Machine-Learning Models Using Multidimensional Habitats MRI Features for Assessing Recurrence and Metastasis Risk in Locally Advanced Nasopharyngeal Carcinoma
abstract: Abstract Background Approximately 30%–40% of patients with locally advanced nasopharyngeal carcinoma (LANPC) develop local recurrence or distant metastasis. Early identification of high-risk patients is therefore important for improving prognosis. Methods A total of 1,285 patients with LANPC from three medical centers were enrolled. Patients from center A were randomly divided into a training set (n = 693) and a validation set (n = 297) at a ratio of 7:3, while patients from centers B and C were combined as an external test set (n = 295). Ten independent machine learning models and 26 stacked ensemble models were developed. Model performance was evaluated using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, precision, and F1 score. The incremental value of multidimensional habitat (MH) features over clinical features alone was assessed using integrated discrimination improvement (IDI), net reclassification improvement (NRI), calibration curves, and decision curve analysis (DCA). The SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) method was used to interpret the final model. Results After recursive feature elimination (RFE), four selected clinical features, namely N category, treatment, platelet count (PLT), and smoking status, were identified and further combined with two imaging features, namely multidimensional habitats derived from contrast-enhanced T1-weighted imaging (T1C MH) and multidimensional habitats derived from T2-weighted imaging (T2WI MH), for model development. The stacked ensemble model combining support vector machine (SVM), gradient boosting machine (GBM), and logistic regression (LR) achieved the best overall performance, with a mean area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.761 (95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.719–0.798) in the 5-fold cross-validation set, 0.742 (95% CI: 0.679–0.801) in the validation set, and 0.721 (95% CI: 0.660–0.776) in the external test set. Conclusion In conclusion, the stacking model constructed based on SVM, GBM, and LR, integrating MH features and clinical features, demonstrated favorable predictive performance for recurrence and metastasis in LANPC patients, and holds promise as an effective tool for individualized risk assessment. Evidence Level: 3 Technical Efficacy: Stage 2

title: Early-onset adenocarcinoma of the ampullary rectum: a case report
abstract: Abstract Background : Early-onset colorectal cancer can present with nonspecific gastrointestinal symptoms, contributing to delayed diagnosis. Adenocarcinoma arising in the ampullary region of the rectum may pose additional diagnostic and surgical challenges because of its distal location. Case presentation : A 33-year-old man presented with nonspecific gastrointestinal complaints. Colonoscopy demonstrated an exophytic tumor involving the lower and middle ampullary regions of the rectum, with luminal narrowing and contact bleeding. Computed tomography showed rectal wall thickening and mesorectal lymph nodes. Histopathological examination confirmed poorly differentiated adenocarcinoma (G3) with lymphovascular and perineural invasion. The final pathological stage was pT3N0M0, with no metastatic lymph nodes identified. The patient underwent abdominoperineal excision of the rectum with sigmoid colon pull-through and had an uncomplicated early postoperative course. Conclusions : This case emphasizes the need to consider colorectal malignancy in younger adults with persistent or unexplained gastrointestinal symptoms. Prompt endoscopic assessment and histopathological confirmation are essential when symptoms are atypical or persistent. Histological risk features should be integrated with tumor stage when planning postoperative management.

title: Congenital Anomalies at a Nigerian Teaching Hospital: A Retrospective Study, 2016–2018
abstract: Abstract Congenital anomalies continue to be a challenge in neonatal medicine. Improving research and the consequent improvement of prevention and management requires a forensic audit of the frequency of each anomaly in children. This retrospective study covering the years 2016–2018 was undertaken at the University of Calabar Teaching Hospital (UCTH) in Southern Nigeria. The findings from the 438 cases examined revealed 129 anomalies including congenital malformations of the nervous system, circulatory system, respiratory system, digestive system, genital organs/urinary system, musculoskeletal system, cleft lip and cleft palate, and chromosomal abnormalities. Talipes equinovarus, congenital malformation of the heart, and congenital cataract were the three most prevalent anomalies recorded in UCTH. The case files indicated a strong genetic predisposition for these conditions. The majority of anomalies were recorded in outpatients who only visited the hospital for delivery and had missed the benefits of managed antenatal care, where some defects may have been detected through genetic screening and ultrasound scans. The study concluded that there was a significant number of congenital anomalies within the study period.

title: Predicting high-risk HPV infection and genotype co-infection using genital tract microecological and pathogen characteristics: a machine learning study
abstract: Abstract Background Persistent infection with high-risk human papillomavirus (HR-HPV) is the principal cause of cervical cancer and its precursor lesions. Vaginal microecological dysbiosis and genital tract co-infections may influence HR-HPV acquisition, clearance, and persistence. However, quantitative prediction models integrating vaginal microecological indicators, genital tract pathogens, and HR-HPV genotype co-infection patterns remain limited. Methods This retrospective study included 3,403 patients who underwent concurrent HPV genotyping, vaginal microecological assessment, and genital tract pathogen testing at the gynecology outpatient clinic of Hainan Women and Children’s Medical Center between January 2022 and December 2025. Of these, 765 were HR-HPV-positive and 2,638 were HR-HPV-negative. Candidate predictors were selected using univariable analysis, multicollinearity assessment based on the variance inflation factor (VIF ≦ 4), and the Boruta algorithm. Seven machine learning models were developed, and their hyperparameters were optimized using grid search with 10-fold cross-validation within the training set. Classifier chains (C ≦ C) and ensemble classifier chains (ECC) were applied to the multi-label prediction of HR-HPV genotypes. Model predictions were interpreted using SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP). Results In multivariable logistic regression, Ureaplasma urealyticum (UU; aOR = 2.051), Chlamydia trachomatis (CT;aOR = 1.982), severe bacterial vaginosis score (aOR = 1.614), abnormal vaginal pH (aOR = 1.375), and sialidase positivity (aOR = 1.747) were independently associated with HR-HPV positivity (all P < 0.05). The random forest model achieved the best discrimination in internal validation (AUC = 0.772, sensitivity 0.735, F1 = 0.650). For the ulti-label task, eight HR-HPV genotypes with at least 30 positive cases were included; the ECC model yielded a higher Jaccard score (0.0226) than the independent-label model (0.0190). SHAP identified UU, age, CT, and cocci abundance as leading predictors, whereas a higher Lactobacillus proportion lowered predicted risk. Conclusions Vaginal microecological dysbiosis and genital tract infections were independently associated with HR-HPV positivity. The random forest model showed moderate discrimination, and ECC provided a modest improvement in multi-genotype prediction. These findings may inform risk-based screening, pending external validation.

title: Multimodal Deep Learning Fusion for Lung Cancer Subtype Differentiation from CT and PET Imaging
abstract: Abstract Differential diagnosis between Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer (NSCLC) and Small Cell Lung Cancer (SCLC) represents a critical decision boundary in thoracic oncology, dictating immediate therapeutic pathways. However, conventional single-modality strategies often lack concurrent anatomical and functional comprehension, while traditional multi-modal fusion networks are limited by pixel-level signal suppression and highly disruptive slice-level labeling noise. This paper introduces a unified Hybrid Multiple Instance Learning (MIL) Fusion Framework designed explicitly for automated, patient-level lung cancer differentiation using paired structural Computed Tomography (CT) and metabolic 18F-FDG Positron Emission Tomography (PET) volumes. The proposed architecture employs independent, parallel EfficientNet-B0 encoders to preserve native modality topologies, utilizing a parameterized multi-head cross-attention mechanism to dynamically map complex non-linear inter-modality dependencies. To bypass the historic constraint of tedious manual slice-by-slice segmentations, an attention-gated MIL pooling bottleneck is integrated to aggregate 3D volumetric slice sequences into cohesive patient-level bags, optimizing learning parameters directly from high-level clinical diagnoses. Rigorous evaluation on the open-source Lung-PET-CT-Dx dataset across a verified, highly stratified cohort of 355 patients (284 training, 71 validation) demonstrates that the proposed framework significantly outperforms baseline paradigms. The optimized hybrid network achieves a prominent patient-level accuracy of 0.7887, a Balanced Accuracy of 0.5536, an Area Under the ROC Curve (AUC) of 0.6607, and a Macro F_1-score of 0.5443. Crucially, architecture actively overcomes severe epidemiological class skew to recover the aggressive minority target, establishing a non-zero SCLC recall of 37.50% while operating at a rapid inference latency of 1.71 ms per slice equivalent. These empirical outcomes demonstrate the system's potential viability as an explainable, high-throughput radiology decision-support tool for accelerated clinical triage.

title: Pelvic Incidence and Iliac Venous Anatomy at L5–S1: A Radiologic Morphometric Study
abstract: Abstract Purpose The vein-free vascular corridor is an important anatomical factor influencing anterior access to the lumbosacral junction. This study aimed to characterize iliac venous anatomy at L5–S1 and its relationship with pelvic incidence (PI), focusing on corridor configuration and dimensions. Methods A consecutive cohort of 160 adults with standing full-spine radiographs and lumbosacral magnetic resonance imaging was analyzed. On axial images at L5–S1, the relationship between the iliac veins and anterior disc was assessed using a five-type classification of the vein-free vascular corridor. Corridor dimensions were quantified as the interiliac distance relative to total disc width. Associations with PI were assessed using linear and ordinal logistic regression, adjusted for age and sex. Results Mean age was 56.8 ± 15.2 years and mean PI was 52.8 ± 12.4°. Types III–IV accounted for 79.4% of cases. Disc window percentage increased progressively across vascular types, from 0% in Type 0 to 79.8% in Type IV (p < 0.001). PI was positively associated with disc window percentage, and this remained significant after adjustment for age and sex (adjusted β = 0.45 percentage points per degree; 95% CI 0.13–0.77; p = 0.006). Increasing PI was also associated with higher vascular corridor categories (adjusted OR 1.028 per degree; 95% CI 1.002–1.054; p = 0.037). Conclusion Pelvic incidence is associated with iliac venous anatomy at L5–S1. Increasing PI was associated with a wider vein-free vascular corridor and with progressively higher corridor categories, supporting a relationship between pelvic morphology and the transverse configuration of the iliac veins.

title: Combined hysteroscopic guided laparoscopic resection for misdiagnosed recurrent high sigmoid colovaginal fistula secondary to sigmoid diverticulitis: A case report
abstract: Abstract Background Sigmoid colovaginal fistula (SVF) is a rare high vaginal fistula easily misdiagnosed as common rectovaginal fistula (RVF) due to identical vaginal flatus and fecal leakage, which frequently causes failed transperineal repair and persistent recurrence. Postoperative anatomical distortion such as pseudocervical ostium further interferes routine digital rectal examination and colposcopy diagnosis. Multidisciplinary team (MDT) combined dual-endoscopic minimally invasive repair for misdiagnosed recurrent high SVF has rarely been reported. Case presentation A 57-year-old postmenopausal female presented with continuous vaginal gas and feculent discharge 6 months after failed transperineal RVF repair. Routine colposcopy with rectal methylene blue test revealed blue fluid leaking from a pseudocervical ostium at posterior vaginal fornix. Pelvic MRI combined with colonoscopy confirmed a 1.5 cm fistulous tract originating from a 0.6×0.8 cm sigmoid diverticulum 25 cm above the anal verge. Endoscopic titanium clip closure of the fistula orifice failed intracolonoscopically. Intervention & Outcomes Preoperative MDT reclassified the diagnosis from recurrent RVF to diverticular high SVF. Intraoperative hysteroscopic transillumination was applied to precisely locate the fistula tract under laparoscopic visualization. Complete fistula resection, sigmoid diverticulectomy and primary colorectal anastomosis were performed simultaneously. The patient recovered uneventfully and was discharged on postoperative day 5. No vaginal fistula recurrence was observed at 6-month follow-up, with significant improvement of fecal incontinence-related quality of life. Conclusion Recurrent high sigmoid colovaginal fistula originating from sigmoid diverticulitis is highly prone to misdiagnosis as RVF, especially in patients with post-surgical vaginal fornix deformation. MDT multimodal imaging combined with colonoscopic staining is mandatory for differential diagnosis. Combined hysteroscopic transillumination and laparoscopic resection serves as a safe, accurate minimally invasive strategy for complex misdiagnosed SVF and reduces reoperation failure risk.

title: Successful Kidney Transplantation from a Living Donor with Double Inferior Vena Cava and Three Renal Veins: Case Report and Literature Review
abstract: Abstract Background: Vascular anomalies in living kidney donors pose technical challenges. Double inferior vena cava (D-IVC) occurs in 0.2%–0.7%, and multiple renal veins in 3%–14%. Their combination is exceptionally rare. Case Report: We report successful living donor transplantation from a 49‑year‑old male with D‑IVC and three left renal veins, donated to his daughter with End-stage renal disease (ESRD). Preoperative Computed tomography angiography (CTA) suggested a prominent gonadal vein; intraoperatively, D‑IVC was confirmed. Three short, distant veins could not be merged; each was individually anastomosed to the external iliac vein. Cold ischemia was 20 minutes. Both recovered uneventfully with excellent graft function. Literature Review: We synthesized 15 high‑quality publications (2020–2025) on epidemiology, surgical strategies, and outcomes. CTA with 3D reconstruction is the gold standard (sensitivity 98%). Options include vein grafts or individual anastomoses. One‑year graft survival (94.2% vs. 95.1%) and donor outcomes are comparable to conventional anatomy. Conclusions: D‑IVC with triple renal veins is not an absolute contraindication. With meticulous imaging and tailored techniques, excellent outcomes are achievable.

title: Surgical difficulty and factors associated with conversion to thoracotomy after neoadjuvant chemoimmunotherapy for non-small cell lung cancer: a single- center retrospective study
abstract: Abstract Background: Neoadjuvant chemoimmunotherapy can produce substantial tumor regression in resectable or potentially resectable non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), but treatment-related inflammation, fibrosis, and hilar adhesions may increase technical surgical difficulty. Methods: We retrospectively analyzed 101 patients with NSCLC who underwent surgery after neoadjuvant chemoimmunotherapy at a single center. Thirty-four patients completed video-assisted thoracoscopic surgery (VATS) and 67 underwent conversion to thoracotomy. Results: In the principal Firth penalized multivariable analysis, cT3-4 disease (OR 34.33, 95% CI 7.84–150.22), pulmonary artery relationship grade (OR 2.03 per grade, 95% CI 1.09–3.79), and bronchial relationship grade (OR 3.25 per grade, 95% CI 1.35–7.82) were associated with conversion. The cT3-4 estimate should be interpreted cautiously because of sparse non-conversion observations. Pulmonary artery and bronchial grades were also associated with longer operative time. Conversion was associated with longer operative time, greater blood loss, and longer chest tube duration, whereas no statistically significant differences were observed in R0 resection or pulmonary complication rates. Conclusions: Higher clinical T stage and more complex pulmonary artery and bronchial relationships on CT were associated with conversion and technical surgical difficulty after neoadjuvant chemoimmunotherapy. Preoperative assessment of local tumor extent and hilar anatomy may assist operative planning; conversion should be interpreted as a potential intraoperative safety strategy rather than automatically as failure of minimally invasive surgery.

title: Association of intratumoral and peritumoral apparent diffusion coefficients with stromal tumor-infiltrating lymphocyte levels in primary triple-negative breast cancer: a retrospective 3-T MRI study
abstract: Abstract Background Tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes (TILs) are associated with treatment response and prognosis in triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC), but their assessment requires tissue sampling. We investigated whether routine pretreatment imaging findings, particularly intratumoral and peritumoral apparent diffusion coefficient (ADC) measurements on 3-T breast MRI, were associated with stromal TIL levels and evaluated an exploratory MRI-based model. Methods This single-center retrospective study included 79 consecutive women with primary TNBC assessed between November 2016 and October 2023. High TIL status was defined as stromal TILs ≥ 10% in pretreatment biopsy specimens. Mammographic, ultrasonographic, MRI, and ¹⁸F-fluorodeoxyglucose PET/CT findings were analyzed when available. A prespecified MRI-based logistic regression model included intratumoral ADC, peritumoral ADC, and MRI margin. Discrimination was assessed by receiver operating characteristic analysis and internally validated using 1,000 bootstrap resamples. Associations with pathological complete response (pCR) were explored. Results High TIL status was present in 57 of 79 participants (72.2%). Among 76 participants with MRI, higher intratumoral ADC (adjusted odds ratio [OR], 6.96; 95% confidence interval [CI], 2.47–19.67; p < 0.001) and lower peritumoral ADC (adjusted OR, 0.27; 95% CI, 0.11–0.66; p = 0.004) were independently associated with high TIL status. The exploratory MRI-based model had an apparent area under the curve (AUC) of 0.934 (95% CI, 0.879–0.989) and an optimism-corrected AUC of 0.914. Intratumoral ADC alone had an AUC of 0.856 (95% CI, 0.768–0.944). The associations remained consistent after adjustment for the MRI system and in the analysis restricted to the predominant Ingenia 3.0T system. In exploratory analyses, pCR was more frequent in participants with high versus low TIL status (58.1% vs. 7.7%; p = 0.001) and in those with high versus low intratumoral ADC (57.1% vs. 8.3%; p = 0.003). Conclusions Routine intratumoral and peritumoral ADC measurements were associated with high stromal TIL status in this single-center TNBC cohort. The exploratory MRI-based model showed good discrimination after bootstrap correction. External multicenter evaluation is required before clinical use.

title: A Multi-Stage Optimized Framework for Fundus Image Classification in Diabetic Retinopathy
abstract: Abstract Diabetic retinopathy (DR) is a progressive retinal disease and is a major contributor to irreversible blindness in diabetic patients globally. Recognizing retinal lesions early and correctly will be vital to preventing vision impairment and for timely clinical intervention. This study introduces an intelligent optimization-based framework for automated detection of diabetic retinopathy, where Improved Grey Wolf Optimization (IGWO) is used to preprocess the retinal images, Improved Whale Optimization Algorithm (IWOA) to segment lesions in the retinal images, Improved Artificial Bee Colony (IABC) to select features from the retinal images, and an Improved Fuzzy Support Vector Machine (IFSVM) to detect the diabetic retina. First, the images of the retina undergo enhancement for image contrast, reduction of noise and illumination variations with IGWO. The improved images are then segmented applying IWOA for precise estimation of the lesion regions. The image segments of the lesions are then used to extract comprehensive colour, texture and shape features, which are then optimized using IABC to remove redundant information while retaining highly discriminative features. Lastly, the optimized feature subset is classified by using the proposed IFSVM. The preprocessing stage of IGWO had a PSNR of 38.64 dB, SSIM of 0.986, MSE of 0.0042, entropy of 7.82, contrast improvement index of 2.06 and processing time of 0.78 s. The IWOA segmentation algorithm proposed in this paper achieved a Dice coefficient of 98.42%, IoU of 96.89%, sensitivity of 98.51%, specificity of 98.83%, precision of 98.46%, and overall segmentation accuracy of 98.68%. The IABC algorithm has only 82 informative features (with a feature reduction of 65.6%), and only 6.41s to optimize. The proposed Improved Fuzzy Support Vector Machine demonstrated superior classification accuracy (98.55%), precision (98.48%), recall (98.51%), F1-score (98.49%) and AUC (99.02%) compared to the rest of the conventional machine learning and deep learning methods. The robust performance of the proposed framework was also statistically validated by 5-fold cross validation with a mean accuracy of 98.55% with a standard deviation of 0.13% which resulted in statistically significant p-values less than 0.005 and narrow confidence intervals.

title: Relapsing Multiple Cranial Neuropathies as a Manifestation of Neurosyphilis: A Case Report and Literature Review
abstract: Abstract Neurosyphilis is an infectious disease of the central nervous system caused by Treponema pallidum. Its incidence has been increasing globally. Due to variable clinical presentations, nonspecific symptoms, and diverse latency periods, neurosyphilis is frequently misdiagnosed or missed altogether. It commonly involves a single cranial nerve.We report a rare case of neurosyphilis presenting with multiple cranial nerve involvement as the initial manifestation. The patient was admitted with progressive cranial neuropathies. Comprehensive evaluations, including serologic tests, cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) analysis, and cranial MRI, were conducted. Laboratory findings supported the diagnosis of neurosyphilis, with positive serum and CSF Treponema pallidum antibodies, CSF pleocytosis, and elevated protein levels. MRI revealed abnormal enhancement of multiple cranial nerves. The patient was treated with high-dose intravenous penicillin, resulting in gradual clinical improvement.This case highlights the diagnostic challenges posed by atypical neurosyphilis presentations. By reviewing this rare case and relevant literature, we aim to improve clinicians' awareness of neurosyphilis with polycranial neuritis and promote timely diagnosis and effective treatment.

title: Changes in tumor volume predict overall survival after [177Lu]Lu-DOTATATE in neuroendocrine neoplasm
abstract: Abstract Purpose Peptide receptor radionuclide therapy (PRRT) is a crucial therapy for neuroendocrine neoplasms (NENs). Pre-treatment somatostatin receptor (SSTR) PET determines eligibility for PRRT and can prognosticate overall survival (OS). The prognostic value of an end-of-treatment (EOT) SSTR-PET is underexplored. Methods 132 NEN patients who were treated with PRRT and underwent baseline and EOT SSTR-PET/CTs were retrospectively identified. Tumor lesions were semi-automatically annotated and total tumor volume (TTV), SUV max and SUV mean were derived from both PET scans and relative change in PET parameters were calculated. Associations between PET parameters and OS were assessed with Cox regression and Kaplan-Meier analyses. Results Higher baseline TTV and increased TTV at EOT were significantly associated with shorter OS, while baseline and EOT SUV metrics were not independently associated with OS. Conclusion Increased TTV at baseline and EOT SSTR-PET/CT portends shorter OS in NEN and may guide clinical decision-making.

title: Radioclinical Characteristics, Diagnostic Approaches, and Clinical Outcomes of Abdominal Tuberculosis: A Six-Year Retrospective Study from a Tertiary Hospital in Somalia
abstract: Abstract Background Abdominal tuberculosis (ATB) is one of the most challenging forms of extrapulmonary tuberculosis because of its nonspecific clinical presentation and radiological resemblance to gastrointestinal malignancies and inflammatory bowel diseases. We conducted a Six-year retrospective observational study to evaluate the radioclinical characteristics, diagnostic approaches, and clinical outcomes of patients with abdominal tuberculosis at a tertiary referral hospital in Somalia. Methods This retrospective study included 286 patients diagnosed with abdominal tuberculosis between January 2019 and December 2024. Patients were classified as confirmed ATB when diagnosis was established by histopathology, microbiological culture, GeneXpert MTB/RIF, or a combination of these methods, and as presumed ATB when diagnosis was based on compatible clinical presentation, characteristic radiological findings after exclusion of alternative diagnoses. Demographic characteristics, clinical manifestations, computed tomography (CT) findings, diagnostic procedures, treatment strategies, and clinical outcomes were analyzed using SPSS version 26. Associations between categorical variables were assessed using Pearson's chi-square test, with P < 0.05 considered statistically significant. Results Among the 286 patients, 226 (79.0%) had confirmed abdominal tuberculosis, while 60 (21.0%) were classified as presumed cases. The majority were young adults, with the highest proportion belonging to the 20–39-year age group. Multiple-site abdominal involvement was the predominant radiological pattern (236/286, 82.5%), followed by isolated peritoneal tuberculosis (47/286, 16.4%). Paracentesis was the most frequently performed diagnostic procedure (186/286, 65.0%). title: New-Onset Continuous Urinary Incontinence After Ectopic Ureteral Stone Surgery with Pre-existing Stress Urinary Incontinence: A Case Report
abstract: Abstract Background: Adult ectopic ureter is uncommon and may be overlooked when a common cause of urinary incontinence coexists. Case presentation: A 66-year-old woman had a 2-year history of intermittent urinary leakage during coughing or physical activity. She later developed right flank pain and fever. Computed tomography (CT) demonstrated bilateral duplicated collecting systems and a right upper-pole ectopic ureter opening into the urethra, with an approximately 11×8 mm calculus impacted near its distal opening (Fig. 1A, B). Ureteroscopic lithotripsy relieved the flank pain. Subsequent urodynamic evaluation demonstrated moderate stress urinary incontinence (SUI) (Fig. 1C), and a tension-free vaginal tape (TVT) procedure initially improved the leakage. One month after TVT, however, the leakage changed to continuous urine loss unrelated to coughing, activity, or body position. Repeat urodynamics were normal, and the leaking fluid remained clear during bladder methylene blue instillation. Cystoscopic reassessment and review of the known duplicated anatomy raised suspicion of an ectopic urinary source (Fig. 2A). Laparoscopy confirmed the ectopic right upper-pole ureter (Fig. 2B), which was reimplanted into the bladder. Postoperative retrograde pyelography documented the reconstructed system (Fig. 2C), and the patient no longer experienced urinary leakage. Conclusion: This case illustrates that ectopic ureter may be easily missed when coexisting SUI provides a convincing explanation for urinary leakage. A transition from stress-related intermittent leakage to continuous, position-independent leakage should trigger reassessment of the diagnosis. In patients with a duplicated collecting system, integration of symptom phenotype, urodynamics, dye testing, cystoscopy, and cross-sectional imaging can help identify an ectopic urinary source and avoid diagnostic delay.

title: Deco-CLIP: Dual-Branch Feature Decoupling CLIP for Fine-Grained Zero-Shot Medical Image Analysis
abstract: Abstract The CLIP model has been widely used in the medical field, improving the efficiency of disease screening and diagnosis by establishing feature-level associations between medical images and radiology reports. However, we have found that the contrastive learning strategy of current medical CLIP primarily focuses on distinguishing high-level semantic features. Therefore, it fails to capture the low-level features related to attributes and relational information, limiting performance in fine-grained tasks. To address these limitations, we propose Deco-CLIP to decouple representational features from semantic features. Specifically, the image modality consists of two Vision Transformer (ViT) encoders that extract semantic and texture features using different pretraining strategies. The text modality consists of a text encoder with dual branches to focus on tokens representing high- and low-level features. Furthermore, to enhance the model's ability to capture fine-grained features, we propose a threshold-adaptive sample mining strategy based on intra-modal similarity, which clusters semantically similar samples into mini-batches. Then, secondary contrastive learning is applied within the mini-batch to align the fine-grained features between image and text modalities. Additionally, a regularized attention mechanism is proposed to guide the two branches of the text encoder to focus on distinct feature representations. We evaluated Deco-CLIP on fine-grained zero-shot tasks, including multi-abnormality detection and report-to-volume retrieval. The results showed a 10.2\% improvement in accuracy for multi-abnormality detection and a 16.2\% increase in recall for report-to-volume retrieval, demonstrating the effectiveness of Deco-CLIP in fine-grained medical tasks. The code will be publicly released.

title: Intralymphatic Blood Flow in Secondary Lymphedema: A Novel Finding and Its Clinical Implications – A Case Report
abstract: Abstract Background Intact lymphatic vessels maintain strict blood-lymphatic segregation. While pathological blood-lymphatic mixing occurs in genetic animal models, spontaneous intralymphatic blood filling has not been clinically documented. Methods A 55-year-old woman with secondary upper-extremity lymphedema following mastectomy presented with abnormal blood flow signals within lymphatic lumina on preoperative high-frequency ultrasound. She had chronic aspirin use and developed acute severe hypertension (220/100 mmHg) with extensive cutaneous ecchymosis preoperatively. Six lymphaticovenous anastomoses were performed under microscopy. Results Intraoperative visualization confirmed blood-filled lymphatic vessels, corroborating ultrasound findings. At 3-month follow-up, the corrected edema reduction rate reached 33.68%, with clinically meaningful improvements in body image, symptom, and mood subdomains of the LYMQOL-Arm scale. Conclusions This represents the first clinical evidence of intralymphatic blood filling. We hypothesize acute hypertension exacerbated venous reflux through latent lymphovenous communications, while aspirin disrupted physiological platelet-mediated blood-lymphatic segregation. LVA remains feasible when intraoperative assessment confirms higher intralymphatic pressure and favorable flow directionality, though single-case limitations apply.

title: Pulmonary non-tuberculous mycobacterial disease masquerading as recurrent tuberculosis in Nigeria: diagnostic complexities and therapeutic challenges from a 17-year longitudinal case report
abstract: Abstract Background Pulmonary non-tuberculous mycobacterial disease (NTM-LD) is increasingly recognised as an important cause of chronic pulmonary infection worldwide. However, in tuberculosis (TB)-endemic settings, NTM-LD remains underdiagnosed because clinical algorithms and laboratory services are primarily designed to detect Mycobacterium tuberculosis. Consequently, patients are frequently misdiagnosed, receive repeated empirical anti-tuberculosis treatment, and experience delays in appropriate management. Case presentation We report a 17-year longitudinal case of an immunocompetent Nigerian man whose chronic respiratory illness ultimately proved to be pulmonary NTM disease. The patient had previously completed treatment for pulmonary tuberculosis in 2004 and presented to the University of Port Harcourt Teaching Hospital in 2009 with chronic productive cough, low-grade fever, weight loss, drenching night sweats, and exertional dyspnoea. Chest radiography demonstrated extensive unilateral fibrocavitary lung disease, while three sputum specimens were negative for acid-fast bacilli (AFB). Based on his clinical history and prevailing national tuberculosis treatment guidelines, he was empirically treated for relapsed pulmonary tuberculosis with a Category II anti-tuberculosis regimen. Despite modest clinical improvement, persistent symptoms and progressive radiographic destruction of the left lung prompted further evaluation. Repeat sputum microscopy detected AFB in one of two specimens, raising suspicion of drug-resistant tuberculosis. Mycobacterial culture performed at the Nigerian Institute of Medical Research yielded a non-tuberculous mycobacterium. Subsequent molecular testing confirmed that the isolate was not a member of the Mycobacterium tuberculosis complex; however, species identification and drug susceptibility testing were unavailable due to diagnostic limitations. Given the extensive cavitary lung disease, chronic pulmonary aspergillosis was also considered, and empirical itraconazole therapy was initiated while further investigations were pursued. The patient subsequently received rifampicin- and clarithromycin-based therapy with gradual clinical improvement. However, irreversible structural lung damage resulted in destroyed left lung syndrome and chronic bronchiectasis requiring long-term respiratory follow-up. Conclusions This case highlights the substantial diagnostic and therapeutic challenges of pulmonary NTM disease in resource-limited, TB-endemic settings. It demonstrates the limitations of relying on AFB microscopy and empirical TB treatment, the importance of recognizing discordant microbiological findings, and the consequences of limited access to mycobacterial species identification and drug susceptibility testing. Strengthening laboratory capacity, integrating NTM into national TB diagnostic algorithms, and improving clinician awareness are essential for facilitating timely diagnosis and appropriate management.

title: Clinical analysis of mycosis fungoides involving the central nervous system：a case report
abstract: Abstract Background Mycosis fungoides (MF) with central nervous system (CNS) involvement is a rare complication of cutaneous T-cell lymphoma(CTCL) without unified diagnostic and therapeutic criteria.We retrospectively analyzed the clinical presentation, diagnostic and therapeutic course, and prognosis of a single case of MF with CNS involvement treated at our institution.Combined neuroimaging, cerebrospinal fluid flow cytometry suggested CNS infiltration, and stereotactic biopsy, histopathology together with positive T-cell receptor gene rearrangement confirmed the diagnosis.This case indicates high vigilance for CNS dissemination in MF patients with new neurological symptoms. It highlights that CNS involvement should be suspected in MF patients with new neurological symptoms, and combined imaging, cerebrospinal fluid testing and biopsy enables timely diagnosis of CNS dissemination in advanced MF. Case Presentation: We report a 49-year-old male with mycosis fungoides (MF) who developed new-onset left facial hypesthesia and left upper limb weakness. Neuroimaging revealed a right frontal lobe lesion with multiple extracranial hypermetabolic foci. Cerebrospinal fluid analysis showed aberrant T-lymphocytes, supporting a diagnosis of MF with central nervous system (CNS) involvement. The patient initially responded to systemic chemotherapy but was subsequently complicated by septic shock and hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis. Two months later, follow-up imaging showed new brain lesions; stereotactic biopsy and positive T-cell receptor gene rearrangement confirmed persistent CNS involvement. Conclusions This case highlights that in MF patients presenting with CNS symptoms,the diagnosis of MF with CNS involvement should be considered and an aggressive diagnostic workup, including imageological assessment, lumbar puncture, tissue biopsy and so on, should be pursued to establish a diagnosis. Therapeutic strategies must be individualized based on each patient's specific disease status.

title: Delayed Diagnosis of Kartagener Syndrome in an Adolescent with Recurrent Sinopulmonary Infections and Severe Bronchiectasis: The First Reported Case from Somalia
abstract: Abstract Background Kartagener syndrome is a rare form of primary ciliary dyskinesia characterized by chronic sinopulmonary disease, bronchiectasis, and situs inversus. Diagnosis is frequently delayed because respiratory manifestations are nonspecific and specialized diagnostic testing may be unavailable, particularly in resource-limited settings. We report what is, to our knowledge, the first reported case of Kartagener syndrome from Somalia, highlighting the diagnostic and management challenges encountered in a resource-limited setting. Case presentation A 15-year-old girl from rural Somalia presented with a lifelong history of recurrent sinopulmonary infections, chronic productive cough, progressive exertional dyspnea, and intermittent hemoptysis. Examination revealed digital clubbing and signs of chronic respiratory disease. Chest radiography and contrast-enhanced computed tomography demonstrated dextrocardia, situs inversus totalis, and extensive bilateral cystic bronchiectasis with superimposed bronchopneumonia. A clinical diagnosis of Kartagener syndrome was made based on the characteristic phenotype, radiological findings, and a PICADAR score of 8/14. Confirmatory investigations, including ciliary function studies and genetic testing, were unavailable because of resource limitations. She was treated with intravenous antibiotics, bronchodilator therapy, and structured airway-clearance therapy, followed by oral azithromycin and daily home-based chest physiotherapy. Family education focused on airway-clearance techniques, recognition of respiratory exacerbations, treatment adherence, and long-term follow-up. Because of the substantial geographic distance from specialist care, follow-up was coordinated with a local primary care physician and supported by telemedicine. At 1 month, her cough and sputum production had markedly decreased, respiratory distress had resolved, and she had returned to school and daily activities. Conclusions Kartagener syndrome should be considered in children and adolescents with recurrent sinopulmonary infections, chronic rhinosinusitis, bronchiectasis, and laterality abnormalities. In resource-limited settings, characteristic clinical and radiological findings can facilitate recognition when definitive diagnostic testing is unavailable, although the limitations of a clinical diagnosis should be acknowledged. Early recognition, sustained airway-clearance therapy, appropriate treatment of respiratory infections, and patient- and family-centered education are important for long-term disease management. This case also illustrates how locally coordinated and remote follow-up may help maintain continuity of care when access to specialized respiratory services is limited.

title: Oral Foregut Duplicate cyst presenting as tongue-tie in a pediatric patient: a clinicopathologic case report
abstract: Abstract Oral foregut duplication cysts (OFDCs) are rare congenital anomalies arising from abnormal foregut development during embryogenesis, characterized by ectopic gastrointestinal or respiratory epithelium within the oral cavity. We present the case of a 6-year-old boy referred to with a presumptive diagnosis of ankyloglossia ("tongue-tie") who was found to have a well-circumscribed midline cystic mass within the intrinsic muscles of the tongue. MRI demonstrated a homogeneous T2-hyperintense, T1-isointense lesion with increased diffusivity and minimal wall enhancement. The mass was excised via a ventral tongue approach and delivered intact. Histopathologic examination revealed a cyst wall lined by ciliated respiratory-type epithelium with an underlying smooth muscular layer, consistent with an oral foregut duplication cyst. The differential diagnosis, including ranula, leiomyoma, rhabdomyoma, and malignant peripheral nerve sheath tumor, is discussed. This case highlights the importance of considering foregut duplication cysts in the differential diagnosis of congenital tongue masses, particularly when clinical presentation mimics ankyloglossia. Complete surgical excision is curative, with a low risk of recurrence.

title: Application Effects of Modified Coronectomy in Mandibular Third Molars with High-Risk Proximity to the Mandibular Canal and Characteristics of Residual Root Migration
abstract: Abstract Objective To evaluate the perioperative outcomes, the protective effect on the inferior alveolar nerve, and the migration characteristics of residual roots within 12 months postoperatively following a modified coronectomy in cases of high-risk contact between the mandibular third molar root and the mandibular canal. Materials and Methods The study included 73 patients treated at the Department of Stomatology, First Affiliated Hospital of the Army Medical University, from November 2023 to July 2025. All patients underwent preoperative cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT) scans and were divided into three groups based on the surgical procedure performed: the exodontia group (33 patients), the coronectomy group (5 patients), and the modified coronectomy group (35 patients). The primary outcome was postoperative sensation in the lower lip and chin, secondary outcomes included operative time, intraoperative blood loss, postoperative pain, facial swelling, limited mouth opening, temporomandibular joint clicking, and residual root migration. Clinical and radiographic follow-up lasted up to 12 months. Results The operative time in the modified coronectomy group was 51.30 ± 19.63 min, which was longer than the 32.97 ± 13.81 min in the exodontia group (P < 0.001); intraoperative blood loss was 15.07 ± 7.03 mL and 10.42 ± 5.88 mL, respectively (P < 0.05); Visual Analog Scale (VAS) scores on postoperative day 3 were 2.50 ± 0.75 and 3.09 ± 1.35, respectively (P < 0.05). No inferior alveolar nerve injury was observed in the modified coronectomy group, whereas the incidence in the exodontia group was 12.12% (P < 0.001); associated sensory abnormalities resolved approximately 3 months postoperatively. Residual root displacement increased with extended follow-up. At 12 months postoperatively, the migration distances for the groups with residual root lengths of ≤ 5 mm, 5–10 mm, and > 10 mm were 4.82 ± 0.59 mm, 3.06 ± 0.81 mm, and 4.13 ± 0.75 mm. After stratification by root morphology, the fusion root group exhibited more pronounced migration in the later stages, while the single-root group showed the lowest migration at 12 months. Conclusion In this study, no inferior alveolar nerve injury was observed in the modified coronectomy group, and postoperative pain scores were low. However, this procedure involved a longer operative time and relatively higher intraoperative blood loss. Residual root migration may be related to residual root length and root morphology, with 5–10 mm residual roots exhibiting relatively better stability during the 12-month follow-up period. Clinical Implications: For mandibular third molars where the root is closely associated with the mandibular canal and complete extraction may increase the risk of inferior alveolar nerve injury, modified coronectomy can serve as an alternative treatment strategy. During surgery, attention should be paid to the complete removal of enamel, control of residual root length, and preservation of alveolar bone, and standardized postoperative follow-up should be implemented.

At 12 months postoperatively, the migration distances for the groups with residual root lengths of ≤ 5 mm, 5–10 mm, and > 10 mm were 4.82 ± 0.59 mm, 3.06 ± 0.81 mm, and 4.13 ± 0.75 mm. After stratification by root morphology, the fusion root group exhibited more pronounced migration in the later stages, while the single-root group showed the lowest migration at 12 months. Conclusion In this study, no inferior alveolar nerve injury was observed in the modified coronectomy group, and postoperative pain scores were low. However, this procedure involved a longer operative time and relatively higher intraoperative blood loss. Residual root migration may be related to residual root length and root morphology, with 5–10 mm residual roots exhibiting relatively better stability during the 12-month follow-up period. Clinical Implications: For mandibular third molars where the root is closely associated with the mandibular canal and complete extraction may increase the risk of inferior alveolar nerve injury, modified coronectomy can serve as an alternative treatment strategy. During surgery, attention should be paid to the complete removal of enamel, control of residual root length, and preservation of alveolar bone, and standardized postoperative follow-up should be implemented.

title: Orbital Complications Following Acute Rhinosinusitis in Children: Clinical Outcomes Across Chandler Classification Stages
abstract: Abstract Purpose Periorbital and orbital cellulitis represent a spectrum of paediatric infections associated with potentially serious complications. Although widely used, the Chandler classification has limited evidence supporting its role in predicting disease severity and guiding management in children. This study evaluated the clinical utility of the Chandler classification and explored a preliminary risk stratification model for severe disease. Methods This retrospective observational cohort study included patients aged under 18 years admitted with periorbital or orbital cellulitis between January 2023 and December 2025. Patients were classified according to Chandler stages I–IV. Demographic, clinical, microbiological, radiological and outcome data were extracted from electronic records. Pearson’s chi-square tests and ordinal logistic regression were used to identify associations and independent predictors of severe disease. Results Eighty-six patients were included: 87.2% had Chandler stage I disease, 2.3% stage II, 5.8% stage III and 4.7% stage IV. Time from presentation to CT imaging demonstrated the strongest association with Chandler stage (χ² = 90.78, p < 0.001), followed by surgical management, nasal steroid use and sinus involvement. Ophthalmoplegia and proptosis were strongly associated with advanced disease. In dichotomised analyses comparing mild (stages I–II) and severe disease (stages III–IV), time to CT imaging showed the largest effect size. Exploratory regression analyses identified admission duration as independently associated with increasing Chandler stage, while age and admission duration were independently associated with severe disease in the dichotomised analysis. Conclusions The Chandler classification differentiates disease severity in paediatric orbital infections and may support early recognition of patients requiring escalated care.

title: Deficient Mismatch Repair, Mucinous Histology, and Systemic Inflammation Are Associated with Nodal Overstaging on Preoperative Computed Tomography in Right-Sided Colon Cancer: A Propensity Score–Matched Study
abstract: Abstract Background Accurate preoperative nodal staging is increasingly important as neoadjuvant immunotherapy emerges for mismatch repair-deficient (dMMR) colon cancer. CT-based N-overstaging may be more frequent in dMMR than in mismatch repair-proficient (pMMR) tumors; however, because dMMR status, mucinous histology, and systemic inflammation often coexist in right-sided colon cancer, we assessed their associations with nodal misclassification. Methods We retrospectively reviewed patients who underwent resection for right-sided colon adenocarcinoma. Patients with dMMR tumors were propensity score–matched to those with pMMR tumors based on age and sex, with exact matching on pT, pN, and mucinous histology. Clinicopathological, molecular, and inflammation-related factors were evaluated using logistic regression. Results The matched cohort comprised 80 dMMR and 78 pMMR patients. Among 106 pathologically node-negative patients, N-overstaging occurred in 29 (53.7%) dMMR and 19 (36.5%) pMMR tumors ( P = 0.076). After multivariable adjustment, dMMR status (adjusted odds ratio [aOR], 2.49; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.02–6.11; P = 0.046), mucinous histology (aOR, 4.65; 95% CI, 1.02–21.24; P = 0.047), and modified Glasgow Prognostic Score (mGPS) 1–2 vs 0 (aOR, 5.42; 95% CI, 1.87–15.75; P = 0.002) were associated with N-overstaging. Among 52 pathologically node-positive patients, N-understaging was less frequent in dMMR than pMMR tumors (11.5% vs 34.6%; P = 0.048), and elevated mGPS was associated with lower odds of N-understaging ( P = 0.030). Conclusions dMMR status, mucinous histology, and elevated mGPS emerged as independent indicators of CT-based N-overstaging in right-sided colon cancer. These tumor- and host-related factors may inform preoperative nodal assessment.

title: A CT-Based and Serum-Derived Nomogram for Preoperative Prediction of Lymphovascular Invasion in Stage Ⅰ Lung Adenocarcinoma
abstract: Abstract Background Lymphovascular invasion (LVI) is a crucial prognostic factor in stage I lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD), yet it can only be confirmed postoperatively. This study aimed to develop a preoperative predictive model for LVI by integrating hematological, clinical, and CT-based radiological features. Methods We retrospectively analyzed 800 patients with stage I LUAD who underwent curative resection. Least Absolute Shrinkage and Selection Operator (LASSO) regression and multivariate logistic regression were employed to identify independent predictors. A nomogram was constructed and internally validated via bootstrap resampling. Model performance was assessed using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), calibration curves, and decision curve analysis (DCA). Results Six independent predictors were identified: neuron-specific enolase (NSE), tumor diameter, consolidation tumor ratio (CTR) > 0.5, spiculation, vacuolar sign, and vessel convergence sign. The nomogram demonstrated good discrimination, with AUCs of 0.841 (95% CI: 0.807–0.875) in the training cohort and 0.786 (95% CI: 0.704–0.868) in the validation cohort. Calibration curves showed excellent agreement between predicted and observed probabilities, and DCA confirmed clinical net benefit across a wide threshold range (5%–80%). Conclusion This simple nomogram incorporating routine CT features and serum NSE offers a robust, noninvasive tool for preoperative individualized prediction of LVI in stage I LUAD, potentially aiding in risk stratification and treatment planning.

title: MESNet: A Lightweight Transformer-CNN Collaborative Network with Morphology Awareness for Glioma Segmentation
abstract: Abstract Glioma segmentation is of great significance for clinical diagnosis and treatment, in which the effective utilization of multimodal information is crucial. Accurate segmentation holds substantial clinical value for guiding precise surgical resection, formulating personalized radiotherapy plans, and assessing prognosis. However, most existing methods focus primarily on the extraction and selection of deep semantic features while overlooking morphologically meaningful features such as edges and shapes. To address this issue, we propose a lightweight high-performance network named MESNet (Morphological Edge and Shape Network). MESNet is a Transformer–CNN collaborative segmentation model that explicitly imposes edge consistency and shape regularity to introduce morphological constraints, thereby enabling precise brain tumor segmentation. The model adopts an efficient 3D Transformer as its backbone, organically integrating convolutional neural networks to capture local details. Through deep complementarity between global context and fine-grained representations, it achieves accurate segmentation. To strengthen boundary awareness, a lightweight multi-scale edge-aware module is designed, which utilizes Sobel-based edge enhancement and spatial attention mechanisms to explicitly sharpen tumor boundaries, substantially reducing boundary errors without significantly increasing computational overhead. To accommodate irregular tumor morphology, an attention-guided shape-aware module is constructed; a zero-initialization strategy is employed to maintain training stability, and the module adaptively focuses on variations in tumor scale and shape, markedly improving the segmentation completeness and contour adherence of small targets such as enhancing tumors. Meanwhile, the network adheres to a lightweight design philosophy, strictly controlling parameter counts and computational complexity through channel compression and efficient attention mechanisms. Experimental results on the BraTS2021 dataset demonstrate that MESNet achieves overall segmentation accuracy and boundary agreement comparable to those of state-of-the-art methods while consuming substantially fewer resources, attaining a superior balance between efficiency and performance. The source code is publicly available at https://github.com/tanjia123456/MESNet-main.

title: The Application Value of Ultrasound Soft Markers in the Examination of Common Fetal Chromosomal Aneuploidy Abnormalities: A Retrospective Study
abstract: Abstract Objective To carry out a retrospective cohort study focusing on prevalent soft markers observed in fetal ultrasounds, follow up the incidence of trisomy 21, 18 and 13, and investigate the positive predictive values of single and multiple soft markers for common chromosomal aneuploidy abnormalities. Methods A total of 19,997 pregnant women with ultrasound-detected soft markers underwent non-invasive prenatal testing (NIPT) or amniocentesis for karyotype analysis and evaluation of chromosomal copy number variations, with their pregnancy outcomes subsequently monitored. The risks of trisomy 21, 18, and 13 associated with various ultrasound soft markers were subjected to statistical analysis. Results A total of 5,530 pregnant women underwent amniocentesis directly, while 14,467 cases received non-invasive prenatal testing (NIPT), among which 23 high-risk cases proceeded to further amniocentesis. Out of 19,997 fetuses exhibiting ultrasound soft markers, 105 were identified with common chromosomal aneuploidy changes, including 93 cases of trisomy 21, 11 cases of trisomy 18, and 1 case of trisomy 13. The overall positive detection rate was 0.53%. Based on the incidence of common chromosomal aneuploidy abnormalities relative to the risks associated with amniocentesis, the ultrasound soft markers were classified into two categories: high-risk (≥ 0.5%) and low-risk (<0.5%). Isolated ultrasound soft markers were linked to a 0.46% risk of target chromosomal aneuploidy. Among these, thickened nuchal translucency (NT), absence or hypoplasia of the nasal bone, and ventriculomegaly were associated with higher risks of aneuploidy at 4.25%, 2.28%, and 0.98%, respectively. Other markers such as choroid plexus cyst (CPC), single umbilical artery (SUA), aberrant right subclavian artery (ARSA), and echogenic intracardiac focus (EIF) indicated risks of 0.22%, 0.22%, 0.19%, and 0.06%, respectively. No instances of common fetal chromosomal aneuploidy abnormalities were observed in cases with urinary tract dilation, echogenic bowel, or shortened femur length. The overall risk of fetal chromosomal aneuploidy in fetuses with two ultrasound soft markers was 0.92%, including a risk of 0.12% for those with two low-risk markers. When three or more ultrasound soft markers were present, the risk of target chromosomal aneuploidy increased to 4.82%, compared to a 1.6% risk observed in cases with three or more only low-risk soft markers. Conclusions Chromosomal detection strategies can be selected reasonably based on the varying risks of common chromosomal aneuploidy associated with different ultrasound soft markers according to this study. For pregnant women with high‑risk ultrasound soft markers, amniocentesis for prenatal diagnosis is recommended in genetic counseling regardless of the number of soft markers. Amniocentesis is also recommended for those with three or more ultrasound soft markers. For women with one or two low‑risk ultrasound soft markers, NIPT targeting common aneuploidies can be an option under fully informed consent. In this way, medical resources can be reasonably allocated and utilized.
