title: The Application of Video‑Electroencephalographic Monitoring Combined with Multimodal Imaging in Surgical Management of Secondary Epilepsy in Children
abstract: Abstract Objective To explore the clinical value of video‑electroencephalography (VEEG) coupled with multimodal imaging for pre‑surgical epileptogenic‑zone localization, surgical planning and prognostic evaluation in children with drug‑resistant epilepsy. Methods : A retrospective analysis was performed on 42 pediatric patients who underwent epilepsy surgery. Pre‑operative workup included brain magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), long‑term scalp VEEG, and PET‑CT for selected participants. For diagnostically challenging cases, stereoelectroencephalography (SEEG) depth electrodes or electrocorticography (ECoG) cortical electrodes were implanted to refine epileptogenic‑zone identification. Cortical electrical stimulation (CES) and somatosensory evoked potentials (SEP) were applied to map eloquent brain regions. Intra‑operative cortical electrophysiological monitoring guided lesion resection. Individualized surgical strategies were adopted according to lesion characteristics. Post‑operative follow‑up spanned 1‑4 years, and seizure outcomes were assessed using the modified Engel classification. Results : ① Pre‑operative brain MRI revealed heterogeneous epileptogenic etiologies, most frequently temporal‑lobe signal abnormalities (17 cases) and focal cortical developmental anomalies (12 cases). ② Long‑term VEEG allowed detailed recording of background electroencephalographic rhythms; sleep markedly elevated the yield of interictal epileptiform discharges. Interictal discharges were captured in 35 patients, and spontaneous clinical seizure discharges were successfully recorded in 15 patients. ③ Among 21 patients receiving PET‑CT, focal hypometabolism was observed within most lesion territories. ④ Combined long‑term VEEG with intracranial SEEG/ECoG electrodes precisely delineated discharge onset zones, while functional‑mapping techniques ensured operative safety. ⑤ Ten distinct individualized surgical protocols were implemented tailored to underlying pathology. Intra‑operative ECoG detected sharp‑wave activity in 35 patients, informing the extent of surgical resection. ⑥ Integrating MRI findings with post‑surgical histopathology clarified the etiological diagnosis for all patients. ⑦ After 1‑4 years of follow‑up, 33 patients attained Engel class I outcomes, indicating satisfactory overall seizure control. Note: Developmental anomalies encompass structural malformations and signal alterations, collectively termed cortical developmental abnormalities herein. Conclusions :Video‑electroencephalography combined with multimodal imaging including MRI and PET‑CT enables reasonably accurate (though not absolute) dual anatomical‑electrophysiological localization of epileptogenic zones. This multimodal framework provides robust evidence for individualized surgical planning and bears considerable clinical utility.

For diagnostically challenging cases, stereoelectroencephalography (SEEG) depth electrodes or electrocorticography (ECoG) cortical electrodes were implanted to refine epileptogenic‑zone identification. Cortical electrical stimulation (CES) and somatosensory evoked potentials (SEP) were applied to map eloquent brain regions. Intra‑operative cortical electrophysiological monitoring guided lesion resection. Individualized surgical strategies were adopted according to lesion characteristics. Post‑operative follow‑up spanned 1‑4 years, and seizure outcomes were assessed using the modified Engel classification. Results : ① Pre‑operative brain MRI revealed heterogeneous epileptogenic etiologies, most frequently temporal‑lobe signal abnormalities (17 cases) and focal cortical developmental anomalies (12 cases). ② Long‑term VEEG allowed detailed recording of background electroencephalographic rhythms; sleep markedly elevated the yield of interictal epileptiform discharges. Interictal discharges were captured in 35 patients, and spontaneous clinical seizure discharges were successfully recorded in 15 patients. ③ Among 21 patients receiving PET‑CT, focal hypometabolism was observed within most lesion territories. ④ Combined long‑term VEEG with intracranial SEEG/ECoG electrodes precisely delineated discharge onset zones, while functional‑mapping techniques ensured operative safety. ⑤ Ten distinct individualized surgical protocols were implemented tailored to underlying pathology. Intra‑operative ECoG detected sharp‑wave activity in 35 patients, informing the extent of surgical resection. ⑥ Integrating MRI findings with post‑surgical histopathology clarified the etiological diagnosis for all patients. ⑦ After 1‑4 years of follow‑up, 33 patients attained Engel class I outcomes, indicating satisfactory overall seizure control. Note: Developmental anomalies encompass structural malformations and signal alterations, collectively termed cortical developmental abnormalities herein. Conclusions :Video‑electroencephalography combined with multimodal imaging including MRI and PET‑CT enables reasonably accurate (though not absolute) dual anatomical‑electrophysiological localization of epileptogenic zones. This multimodal framework provides robust evidence for individualized surgical planning and bears considerable clinical utility.

title: Structured Modality Dropout for Robust MRI-Based IDH Mutation Classification in Glioma
abstract: Abstract The classification of IDH gene mutation is an essential marker in the treatment of a group of brain tumors called glioma, indicating the favorability of prognosis and response to treatment. Current methods determine the IDH mutation status invasively through postoperative tissue and DNA analysis. It is favorable to predict the mutation status non-invasively from MRI scans to determine suitable surgical strategies. Existing MRI-based prediction models often assume the availability of all four MRI modalities. However, in real-world clinical settings, one or more modalities may be missing due to reasons such as image quality and inconsistent protocols. This severely impacts the performance of MRI-based deep learning models. This study proposes a structured modality dropout training strategy to improve the robustness of a 3D ResNet18 model for IDH prediction. We compared three training strategies: Baseline (no dropout), Dropout-30 (moderate), and Dropout-50 (aggressive). All three models were evaluated using five-fold stratified cross-validation across six realistic modality availability scenarios (all four, missing T1CE, missing FLAIR, missing T2, T1 and T2 only, T1 only). Performance was evaluated using area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC-ROC), balanced accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, Brier score, and bootstrap confidence intervals (CI). Key Findings: The Baseline model performed best when all four modalities were available (AUC $0.823 \pm 0.042$), but the Dropout models showed more stable performance as the number of missing modalities increased. The Dropout-30 model showed the best calibration, with the lowest Brier score of $0.198$. Overall, Dropout-30 was the most balanced and clinically viable model, remaining the most stable across scenarios, best calibrated, and showing good generalization across scanner models.

title: Methodology of a prospective, single-arm, multicenter, physician-initiated study to assess the long-term safety and efficacy of the Restorer stent system for the treatment of aorto-iliac lesions. BARISTA trial.
abstract: Abstract Background Evidence regarding optimal stent selection in endovascular treatment of aorto-iliac lesions remains inconclusive, particularly in complex TASC C and D disease. Interpretation of existing data is complicated by study heterogeneity and selection bias. Both bare metal stents (BMS) and covered stents (CS) are widely used, yet comparative evidence remains limited. The BARISTA trial aims to prospectively evaluate the safety and efficacy of the Restorer iliac stent system (iVascular) and to compare its outcomes with those reported in contemporary studies assessing covered stents. Methods Between July 2022 and June 2024, this prospective multicenter study enrolled 200 patients across 14 Belgian centers. The objective is to assess two-year safety and efficacy outcomes of the Restorer iliac stent system in symptomatic aorto-iliac disease. The primary composite endpoint includes: (1) freedom from target lesion revascularization (TLR), (2) freedom from major amputation, and (3) absence of restenosis within 12 months. TLR is defined as any repeat intervention within the treated segment, including 5 mm proximal and distal to the lesion. Restenosis is defined as > 50% stenosis on duplex ultrasound with a systolic velocity ratio > 2.4. Discussion By analyzing outcomes in a large prospective cohort and comparing results with contemporary CS data, the BARISTA trial aims to support evidence-based stent selection in aorto-iliac disease. Trial registration ClinicalTrials.gov ID: NCT05293002 (2022-03-23)

title: Predictive Value of Quantitative T2-Weighted MRI Morphometric Parameters for Clinically Significant Prostate Cancer in PI-RADS v2.1 ≥4 Lesions
abstract: Abstract Objective To evaluate the diagnostic accuracy of quantitative T2-weighted MRI morphometric parameters for detecting clinically significant prostate cancer (csPCa) in prostate lesions with PI-RADS v2.1 category ≥ 4. Methods This retrospective study included 153 patients who underwent multiparametric MRI according to the PI-RADS v2.1 protocol followed by prostate biopsy. A total of 165 prostate lesions with PI-RADS v2.1 scores ≥4were analyzed. Based on histopathological results, lesions were classified as csPCa or benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH). Quantitative morphometric parameters, including maximum diameter, mean diameter, cross-sectional area, and volume, were measured on tri-planar T2-weighted images. Differences between csPCa and BPH lesions, as well as zone-specific characteristics in the peripheral zone (PZ) and transition zone (TZ), were assessed. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis was performed to evaluate the diagnostic performance of each parameter and to determine optimal cutoff values. Results Among the 165 lesions, 108 were csPCa (69 in the PZ and 39 in the TZ) and 57 were BPH (20 in the PZ and 37 in the TZ). csPCa lesions demonstrated significantly larger maximum diameter, mean diameter, area, and volume compared with BPH lesions in both the PZ and TZ (all p < 0.05). ROC analysis showed that lesion volume achieved the highest diagnostic performance among all morphometric parameters, with area under the curve (AUC) values of 0.819 in the PZ and 0.811 in the TZ. The optimal volume thresholds for differentiating csPCa from BPH were 1.23 cm³ in the PZ and 1.07 cm³ in the TZ, respectively. Conclusions In prostate lesions with PI-RADS v2.1 category ≥ 4, lesion volume demonstrates superior diagnostic accuracy compared with maximum diameter, mean diameter, and area. Volume-based assessment may serve as a valuable quantitative imaging biomarker to improve the detection of clinically significant prostate cancer, particularly when accounting for zone-specific differences.

title: Longitudinal MRI Response Phenotypes and Lesion-Level Local Control after Gamma Knife Radiosurgery for Breast Cancer Brain Metastases
abstract: Abstract Purpose Serial magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) demonstrates heterogeneous lesion evolution after stereotactic radiosurgery. We characterized longitudinal volumetric response phenotypes after Gamma Knife radiosurgery (GKRS) for breast cancer brain metastases and examined their association with 12-month lesion-level local control. Methods This single-center retrospective study included 80 patients, 182 GKRS-treated lesions, and 819 serial MRI records. Local control was assessed within a prespecified 10–14-month window. Lesions were classified as complete response/disappearance, partial regression, stable control, or progression. Baseline correlates of local failure were evaluated using Bayesian mixed-effects logistic regression, with patient-clustered generalized estimating equations used for sensitivity analysis. Results Local control was evaluable in 103 lesions and longitudinal phenotype in 154. The four phenotypes comprised 24 complete responses/disappearances, 59 partial regressions, 44 stable controls, and 27 progressions. In the prespecified Bayesian model, larger baseline whole-tumor volume and peritumoral edema were associated with higher odds of local failure, whereas higher BED₁₀ was inversely associated; clustered sensitivity estimates retained the same directions but were less precise. Progression phenotype was strongly associated with local failure after accounting for within-patient clustering (odds ratio 27.08, 95% confidence interval 7.11–103.20; p < 0.001) and remained associated when classification was restricted to the 10–14-month window. Conclusion Longitudinal volumetric MRI phenotypes capture heterogeneous post-GKRS lesion evolution and identify a progression pattern closely associated with local failure. This framework may complement standard local-control assessment during post-treatment surveillance.

title: PathVista Integrates Cellular Foundation Models with Multiscale Histopathology for Colorectal Cancer Prognosis and Molecular Stratification
abstract: Abstract Personalized management of colorectal cancer (CRC) requires accurate risk stratification and identification of clinically actionable molecular alterations. However, standard clinicopathologic features often fail to capture the cellular and tumor microenvironmental heterogeneity driving disease behavior. Although routine hematoxylin and eosin (H&E) whole-slide images (WSIs) reflect these patterns, patch-level foundation models may obscure fine-grained cellular morphology and spatial organization. We present PathVista , a cell-centered framework that integrates cellular and tissue-level representations for prognostic and molecular stratification. PathVista incorporates CellSwAV , a cellular foundation model pretrained on more than 160 million CRC cells and combines spatially aggregated cellular features with broader tissue context. Across 2,568 CRC patients , PathVista risk scores were significantly associated with overall survival (HR = 6.65, 95% CI: 3.53–12.51) , disease-free survival (HR = 3.15, 95% CI: 1.82–5.45) , and recurrence-free survival (HR = 3.04, 95% CI: 1.76–5.26) , with risk scores remaining independently associated with outcomes after clinicopathologic adjustment. Locked models also generalized to external TCGA (HR = 5.25, 95% CI: 2.29–12.05) and SURGEN (HR = 2.89, 95% CI: 1.86–4.49) cohorts. PathVista predicted microsatellite instability (AUC = 0.91) and BRAF mutation status (AUC = 0.83) . Across 4,667 patients spanning CRC, lung, and breast cancers, PathVista demonstrated the potential of cell-centered histopathology for prognostic, molecular, and tumor characterization.

title: A Nerve Root-Centered Classification System for Lumbar Disc Herniation: Development and Reliability Assessment
abstract: Abstract Background Existing classifications of lumbar disc herniation (LDH) mainly describe disc morphology, migration, or canal compromise, but provide limited information regarding the spatial relationship between the herniated disc and the affected nerve root. This study developed a nerve root-centered classification for patients undergoing percutaneous endoscopic lumbar discectomy (PELD) and evaluated its observer reliability and agreement with intraoperative findings. Methods This single-center retrospective classification-development and reliability study included 516 patients with LDH who underwent PELD between January and December 2022. The Peking University Third Hospital (PUTH) classification integrates the cranio-caudal origin pattern of the affected nerve root (Types 1–3) with the location of the herniated disc relative to the nerve root (Types A–D). Preliminary classifications based on preoperative magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) were compared with consensus reference classifications established through blinded review of intraoperative videos by senior spine surgeons. Intraobserver and interobserver reliability were evaluated by three surgeons from the study institution using all 516 cases and by five surgeons from external institutions using 100 proportionately stratified cases from the same cohort. Clinical outcomes were summarized descriptively after a minimum follow-up of 2 years. Results MRI-based classifications agreed with the consensus video-based reference classifications in 486 of 516 cases (94.2%). Thirty discordant cases were mainly attributable to severe nerve root compression, incomplete visualization of the nerve root origin on MRI, or anatomical variation. Internal intraobserver agreement was substantial to excellent (κ = 0.776–0.842), and internal interobserver agreement was excellent (κ = 0.837). Among external raters, intraobserver agreement was substantial (κ = 0.659–0.756), whereas interobserver agreement was also substantial but lower than that observed internally (κ = 0.645). At final follow-up, lower VAS and ODI scores and a higher JOA score were observed compared with preoperative values. Symptomatic recurrence occurred in 13 patients (2.52%), and postoperative complications occurred in 9 patients (1.74%). Conclusion The PUTH classification demonstrated substantial-to-excellent observer reliability and high MRI–operative agreement in a single-center cohort undergoing PELD. Independent prospective multicenter studies are required to determine its generalizability and influence on surgical decision-making and clinical outcomes.

title: Interpretable Concept-Bottleneck Vision-Language Model Predicts Pathologic Complete Response From Longitudinal Breast DCE-MRI
abstract: Abstract Deep learning can predict neoadjuvant treatment response in breast cancer, but most models are black boxes whose reasoning clinicians cannot verify, limiting adoption. We developed an interpretable concept-bottleneck vision-language model (CB-VLM) that predicts pathologic complete response (pCR) from pre-treatment and early-treatment dynamic contrast-enhanced (DCE) MRI, routing every prediction through eleven radiologist-recognizable, BI-RADS-style imaging concepts plus age and molecular subtype. Trained on 753 patients from the multicenter I-SPY2 trial, the model achieved an AUROC of 0.76 on encoder-held-out data (n = 144) and generalized to an independent I-SPY1 cohort (AUC 0.71; n = 110). Accuracy rose with model confidence (88% versus 58% on borderline predictions), and early change in functional tumor volume was the dominant predictor across both cohorts. To our knowledge, this is the first large vision-language model to generate concept-grounded reasoning for breast DCE-MRI treatment response prediction, reframing a black-box task as transparent, auditable, and generalizable.

title: Development and validation of a three-marker urine DNA methylation assay complementary to mpMRI for pre-biopsy risk stratification of clinically significant prostate cancer
abstract: Abstract Background Current prostate cancer (PCa) diagnostic strategies remain limited in accurately identifying clinically significant disease while avoiding unnecessary biopsy. This study aimed to develop and independently validate a non-invasive urine DNA methylation assay using naturally voided, non-digital rectal examination (non-DRE) urine and assess its complementary value with multiparametric magnetic resonance imaging (mpMRI) for detecting clinically significant prostate cancer (csPCa; Grade Group ≥ 2). Methods The biomarker discovery phase was initiated using microarray-based DNA methylation profiling to screen for tumor-specific alterations, and the candidate regions were subsequently validated by bisulfite-pyrosequencing in the same tissue specimens. Three prioritized markers– CDYL , EMX2 , and LRRC4– were incorporated into a linear target enrichment quantitative methylation-specific PCR assay. Marker-specific thresholds optimized in a training cohort (n = 33) were locked and evaluated in an independent validation cohort of men undergoing biopsy for suspected PCa (n = 97). All participants underwent pre-biopsy mpMRI and standard prostate biopsy. Of the 97 validation patients, 89 were evaluable for combined-modality analysis, while 8 were excluded due to missing mpMRI scans. Results In the training cohort, the assay achieved 100% sensitivity and 31.6% specificity for csPCa. In the independent validation cohort, standalone assay performance yielded 75.9% sensitivity and 44.2% specificity. Among the 89 patients evaluable for both modalities (49 csPCa, 40 no-csPCa), mpMRI alone (PI-RADS ≥ 4) showed a sensitivity of 69.4%. Combining the urine assay and mpMRI using an either-positive strategy significantly increased diagnostic sensitivity to 91.8% ( P < 0.01 vs. mpMRI alone), with a negative predictive value of 78.9%. In an exploratory analysis of the indeterminate PI-RADS 3 subgroup, the urine assay correctly identified all 4 biopsy-confirmed cases of csPCa (100% sensitivity). Conclusions The three-marker non-DRE urine DNA methylation assay demonstrates independent diagnostic performance and complementarity to mpMRI. Integrating this molecular assay with anatomical imaging significantly enhances csPCa detection compared with mpMRI alone. These findings support prospective evaluation of predefined, integrated MRI-urine methylation algorithms to refine pre-biopsy risk stratification and optimize biopsy decision-making.

title: Successful emicizumab prophylaxis in treatment-refractory acquired von Willebrand syndrome associated with rheumatoid arthritis
abstract: Abstract Acquired von Willebrand syndrome (AVWS) is a rare bleeding disorder characterized by acquired quantitative or qualitative abnormalities of von Willebrand factor (VWF) and may occur in association with autoimmune disease. Management can be challenging when conventional hemostatic and immunomodulatory therapies fail. We report a 63-year-old man with longstanding rheumatoid arthritis (RA) and no personal or family history of abnormal bleeding who developed life-threatening hemorrhage following dental extractions, resulting in airway obstruction requiring tracheostomy and red blood cell transfusion. Evaluation demonstrated an isolated prolonged activated partial thromboplastin time, markedly reduced factor VIII (FVIII) activity, profoundly decreased VWF antigen and activity, and no detectable FVIII inhibitor. The late onset of bleeding, negative genetic testing, poor VWF recovery following high-dose VWF/FVIII concentrate, and underlying autoimmune disease supported a diagnosis of AVWS. Severe VWF deficiency persisted despite treatment with rituximab, methotrexate, and intravenous immunoglobulin (IVIG). Emicizumab was subsequently initiated for prophylactic hemostasis. The patient remained free of spontaneous bleeding despite persistent severe reductions in VWF and FVIII measurements and subsequently underwent upper endoscopy with biopsy and colonoscopy without hemorrhagic complications using adjunctive tranexamic acid. To our knowledge, this represents the first reported case of RA-associated AVWS successfully managed with emicizumab prophylaxis. This case demonstrates sustained clinical hemostasis with emicizumab in treatment-refractory AVWS associated with RA and supports further investigation of FVIII-mimetic therapy as a potential prophylactic strategy when conventional therapies are ineffective.

Evaluation demonstrated an isolated prolonged activated partial thromboplastin time, markedly reduced factor VIII (FVIII) activity, profoundly decreased VWF antigen and activity, and no detectable FVIII inhibitor. The late onset of bleeding, negative genetic testing, poor VWF recovery following high-dose VWF/FVIII concentrate, and underlying autoimmune disease supported a diagnosis of AVWS. Severe VWF deficiency persisted despite treatment with rituximab, methotrexate, and intravenous immunoglobulin (IVIG). Emicizumab was subsequently initiated for prophylactic hemostasis. The patient remained free of spontaneous bleeding despite persistent severe reductions in VWF and FVIII measurements and subsequently underwent upper endoscopy with biopsy and colonoscopy without hemorrhagic complications using adjunctive tranexamic acid. To our knowledge, this represents the first reported case of RA-associated AVWS successfully managed with emicizumab prophylaxis. This case demonstrates sustained clinical hemostasis with emicizumab in treatment-refractory AVWS associated with RA and supports further investigation of FVIII-mimetic therapy as a potential prophylactic strategy when conventional therapies are ineffective.

title: A Study on the Application of Multimodal MRI Deep Learning in the Early Detection of Osteonecrosis of the Femoral Head
abstract: Abstract Objective: Osteonecrosis of the femoral head (ONFH) is a debilitating disorder that frequently leads to hip joint dysfunction. Early and accurate diagnosis is crucial to improving clinical outcomes. This study aimed to develop a magnetic resonance imaging (MRI)-based detection model using the You Only Look Once (YOLO) deep learning framework for automatic identification of early-stage ONFH, and to systematically evaluate how different MRI modalities affect detection performance and their potential for clinical decision support. Methods: We retrospectively collected MRI data from 253 ONFH patients across two medical centers, including T1-weighted Imaging (T1WI) and T2-weighted Imaging (T2WI) sequences. After standardized preprocessing, the dataset was partitioned into training, validation, and test sets (7:1:2). Two sequential experiments were conducted. Experiment 1 compared six YOLO generations (v3, v5, v8, v10, v11, v13) using single-center T1WI data, with precision (P), recall (R), mean average precision (mAP), and inference speed as primary metrics. Experiment 2 applied the optimal model to single-modality (T1WI or T2WI) and multimodal fused images from both centers, using the same metrics to quantify detection efficacy and validate multicenter robustness. Results: In Experiment 1, YOLO v11 outperformed all other models, achieving a mAP@0.5 of 0.966, a recall of 0.941, and a per-frame inference time of 4.9 ms. In Experiment 2, the multimodal fusion input (T1WI+T2WI) yielded the highest performance across all modalities, with a mAP@0.5 of 0.9637, a recall of 0.9388, and the fastest inference time (3.0 ms), surpassing both T1WI (R=0.9159, 4.9 ms) and T2WI (R=0.9113, 6.0 ms) alone. Conclusion: The proposed YOLO v11 model demonstrates excellent performance in MRI-based ONFH detection, and the multimodal fusion strategy further improves both diagnostic accuracy and computational efficiency. This approach addresses the dual clinical requirements for high precision and real-time processing, offering a practical and objective intelligent tool for early ONFH screening.

title: Neural correlates of cognitive enhancement after probiotic supplementation
abstract: Abstract A previous randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled clinical trial demonstrated that multistrain probiotic supplementation improved visuospatial cognitive performance in older adults with early cognitive impairment. Participants from a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial (N = 68; probiotic, n = 32; placebo, n = 36) underwent T1-weighted magnetic resonance imaging at baseline and after 52 weeks. Cortical surface area and thickness were quantified using FreeSurfer-based surface morphometry. Between-group differences in longitudinal changes were assessed using t-tests and analysis of covariance adjusted for baseline values and demographic covariates. Compared with placebo, the probiotic group showed increased surface area in the left lingual gyrus (+ 21.53 vs. −54.39 mm², p = 3.12 × 10⁻⁴) and cuneus (+ 5.31 vs. −26.28 mm², p = 0.002). Cortical thickness decreased modestly in these regions in the probiotic group. Structural changes in the lingual gyrus and cuneus were associated with visuospatial cognitive performance. Multistrain probiotic supplementation was associated with region-specific longitudinal cortical changes in the left lingual gyrus and cuneus, particularly in cortical surface area. These morphometric changes were associated with visuospatial cognitive performance in older adults with early cognitive impairment.

title: High-Frequency Ultrasound as a Clinical Tool for Diagnosing Pediatric Anterior Talofibular Ligament Injuries and Guiding Conservative Treatment of Avulsion Fractures
abstract: Abstract Background： Pediatric anterior talofibular ligament (ATFL) injuries differ from those in adults, with avulsion injuries occurring frequently at the ligament attachment sites. Small avulsion fractures may be difficult to detect, while objective imaging parameters for treatment planning and follow-up remain limited. This study evaluated the diagnostic and prognostic utility of high-frequency ultrasound (US) in pediatric ATFL injuries. Methods： We retrospectively analyzed 194 pediatric patients with ATFL injuries who underwent high-frequency US between December 2024 and March 2026. Thirty-two surgically treated patients were included in a diagnostic comparison of US and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), using intraoperative findings as the reference standard. Forty-two patients with ATFL avulsion fractures treated conservatively and followed by US for 3 months were included in the prognostic analysis. The sensitivity and specificity of US and MRI for complete ATFL tears and avulsion fractures were assessed. The avulsion fracture separation distance was measured on US, and its ability to predict healing was evaluated using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis. Measurement reproducibility was assessed using intraclass correlation coefficients (ICCs). Results： Among the 194 patients, avulsion fracture was the predominant injury pattern, occurring in 129 (66.5%). In the surgical cohort, complete ATFL tears were confirmed in 6 patients and avulsion fractures in 26. For complete tears, US showed a sensitivity of 83.3% compared with 66.7% for MRI. For avulsion fractures, US demonstrated 100% sensitivity versus 80.8% for MRI, with 100% specificity for both modalities. Among the 42 conservatively treated patients, 25 (59.5%) demonstrated healing at 3 months. Avulsion fracture separation distance showed excellent predictive performance for healing (AUC, 0.935; 95% CI, 0.814–0.988; P < 0.001). A cutoff of ≤0.95 mm yielded 92.0% sensitivity and 82.4% specificity. Interobserver and intraobserver agreement were excellent (ICC, 0.962 and 0.971, respectively). Conclusions： High-frequency US provides sensitive detection of pediatric ATFL avulsion fractures and enables quantitative assessment of avulsion fracture separation. A separation distance of ≤0.95 mm was associated with a higher likelihood of healing after conservative treatment. High-frequency US may therefore provide orthopedists with practical diagnostic and prognostic information to support treatment planning and follow-up in pediatric ATFL injuries.

title: Snowman-like appearance in spinal capillary hemangioma with combined intra- and extramedullary components: two case reports
abstract: Abstract Background Capillary hemangiomas are benign tumors primarily found in the soft tissues of the head and neck, and their occurrence in the spinal cord is rare. Because of its rarity and nonspecific radiological features, it is often difficult to differentiate from more common intradural-extramedullary tumors. Case presentation: We report two cases of thoracic spinal capillary hemangioma with intra- and extramedullary components. MRI demonstrated strongly and homogeneously enhancing tumors with a snowman-like appearance. Intraoperatively, both tumors were highly vascular, with contiguous intra- and extramedullary components closely associated with the spinal pia mater. The tumors were resected en bloc after control of tumor-related vessels. Histopathological examination demonstrated proliferation of capillary-sized vessels without stromal cells, consistent with capillary hemangioma. Postoperative recovery was uneventful. Conclusion A snowman-like appearance is not necessarily specific to spinal hemangioblastoma and may also occur in spinal capillary hemangioma with combined intra- and extramedullary components. Capillary hemangioma should therefore be considered in the differential diagnosis when this imaging pattern is observed.

title: An Efficient and Explainable CNN-Transformer Architecture for Brain Tumor MRI Classification with Deployment-Oriented Benchmarking
abstract: Abstract Brain tumor classification from MRI is essential for treatment planning, but manual interpretation by radiologists is time-consuming and prone to inter-observer variability. Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) capture local texture effectively but have a limited receptive field, whereas Vision Transformers (ViTs) model global context but require large training datasets and lack spatial inductive bias. Existing hybrid CNN-ViT studies on this task, however, rarely benchmark against classical baselines, report computational costs, provide dual visual explainability, or address the risk of patient-level data leakage. The paper proposes a hybrid architecture that sequentially combines a pretrained ResNet50 backbone with a lightweight Transformer Encoder head, converting intermediate CNN feature maps into visual tokens to jointly model fine-grained local lesion detail and global anatomical context. The model is evaluated on the 7200 image datasets (glioma, meningioma, pituitary tumor, no tumor) using stratified 5-fold cross-validation with statistical significance testing, and it is compared to a PCA-SVM baseline built on the same CNN features to isolate the Transformer’s contribution. Computational efficiency (parameters, FLOPS, latency, peak memory) and dual-level explainability (Grad-CAM for the CNN branch, Attention Rollout for the Transformer branch) are also assessed. The proposed model achieves 97.40% ± 0.24% mean cross-validation accuracy, significantly outperforming the PCA-SVM baseline (paired t-test, p = 2.42 x 10^-5) while requiring only 37.20M parameters and 9.21 GFLOPs, an overhead of only 13.68M additional parameters and 0.95 additional GFLOPS (an 11.5% increase) over the CNN-only backbone. These findings position the proposed framework as an accurate, computationally efficient, and interpretable solution for automated brain tumor MRI classification.

title: Development and Validation of a Machine Learning Model for Predicting Pulmonary Embolism Using Routine Clinical Features
abstract: Abstract Background Pulmonary embolism (PE) is a life‑threatening cardiovascular emergency with non‑specific presentations, making timely diagnosis challenging. Over‑reliance on computed tomography pulmonary angiography (CTPA) has raised concerns about radiation exposure and healthcare costs. Traditional clinical prediction rules, such as the Wells and Geneva scores, have limited specificity and fail to capture complex interactions among risk factors. Machine learning (ML) offers a promising alternative, but many existing models lack interpretability or depend on features not routinely available in emergency settings. Objective To develop and internally validate a parsimonious, interpretable ML model for predicting PE using routinely available clinical variables, and to apply SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) to enhance model transparency. Methods We conducted a retrospective study of 519 patients suspected of PE at a single tertiary referral center. Eight independent predictors—age, hyperlipidemia, limb circumference, D‑dimer, oxygen saturation, dyspnea, immobility, and malignancy—were identified via univariate and multivariable logistic regression on the training set. Three ML algorithms (Lasso, Random Forest, and XGBoost) were trained and evaluated on a 70/30 train‑test split. Model performance was assessed using AUC‑ROC, calibration plots, and Brier score. SHAP analysis was performed for global and local interpretability. Results On the testing set, Lasso achieved an AUC of 0.766 (95% CI: 0.691–0.840), while XGBoost showed a comparable AUC of 0.764 (95% CI: 0.690–0.837). XGBoost was selected as the primary model due to its superior interpretability via SHAP. At the optimal threshold of 0.526, XGBoost achieved a sensitivity of 74.4%, specificity of 66.7%, and overall accuracy of 71.0%. Calibration was moderate (Brier score = 0.224 vs. null model 0.247; Hosmer‑Lemeshow P = 0.563). SHAP analysis identified limb circumference, D‑dimer, and malignancy as the top three contributors to PE risk. Conclusions The XGBoost model based on eight routine clinical features demonstrated moderate discriminative ability and good interpretability for predicting PE. This tool may serve as a decision‑support aid for emergency physicians in risk stratification, potentially reducing unnecessary CTPA utilization. However, the high PE prevalence (55.6%) in our tertiary cohort limits generalizability; external validation in broader, low‑prevalence populations is essential before clinical implementation. Trial registration : Not applicable (retrospective observational study).

title: Investigating renal tissue responses to radiopharmaceutical therapy using multiparametric MRI ​
abstract: Abstract Objectives Renal toxicity is a recognized potential adverse effect of radiopharmaceutical therapy (RPT). While 177 Lu-based therapies are generally well tolerated, subtle therapy-related renal changes remain insufficiently characterized. This study investigated longitudinal renal alterations during 177 Lu-based RPT using multiparametric magnetic resonance imaging (mpMRI) and evaluated its potential for renal monitoring. Methods Twenty-three patients undergoing RPT with either [ 177 Lu]Lu-DOTATATE (n = 14) or [ 177 Lu]Lu-PSMA (n = 9) underwent renal mpMRI examinations before and during therapy with up to four treatment cycles. Imaging included arterial spin labeling, diffusion-weighted imaging with intravoxel incoherent motion analysis, blood oxygenation level-dependent imaging, T1 mapping, and volumetry. Renal scintigraphy, estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR), and absorbed renal radiation dose were assessed longitudinally. Results No significant decline in eGFR was observed during RPT after exclusion of two patients who developed urinary tract obstruction (p = 0.19). Longitudinal analysis revealed significant temporal changes in T1 values (p = 0.008) and perfusion fraction of IVIM (p = 0.005), as well as a modest decrease in the corticomedullary BOLD ratio (p = 0.020). No significant longitudinal changes were detected for other MRI or scintigraphic parameters. Absorbed renal radiation dose was not associated with changes in MRI-derived biomarkers, eGFR, or renal scintigraphy (all p > 0.05). Patients with urinary obstruction demonstrated distinct MRI abnormalities, including reduced renal blood flow (RBF) and altered BOLD metrics. Conclusions No clinically relevant renal functional deterioration or major imaging abnormalities were detected during contemporary 177 Lu-based RPT. Subtle longitudinal T1 increases may reflect mild structural tissue remodeling without measurable functional consequences. Renal mpMRI is feasible for non-invasive monitoring and may provide complementary information beyond conventional renal function assessment. Trial registration, DRKS, DRKS00018966, registered 10 October 2019; https://www.drks.de/search/de/results

title: Diagnosis and treatment of gastric bronchogenic cyst: a case report and literature review
abstract: Abstract Background: Gastric bronchogenic cyst (GBC) is a rare congenital foregut anomaly, typically located near the gastric fundus or cardia. Due to its nonspecific clinical and imaging features, preoperative diagnosis is challenging, and it is often misdiagnosed as a gastrointestinal stromal tumor (GIST) or other submucosal lesions, especially when imaging reveals a solid-appearing or atypical cystic mass. Case presentation: A 42-year-old asymptomatic woman was incidentally found to have a cystic mass adjacent to the gastric cardia. Enhanced CT and MRI revealed a well-defined, approximately 3.0 cm × 2.2 cm lesion with no significant enhancement. Endoscopy showed a smooth-surfaced submucosal elevation. The patient underwent successful laparoscopic complete resection, with careful dissection to preserve the gastric muscular layer and maintain cyst integrity. Histopathological examination confirmed the diagnosis of GBC, characterized by a cyst wall lined with pseudostratified ciliated columnar epithelium. The postoperative course was uneventful, and the patient recovered well with no recurrence at the 3-month follow-up. Conclusion: GBC should be considered in the differential diagnosis of a well-defined, non-enhancing cystic mass near the gastric cardia, particularly when it mimics a GIST. Laparoscopic complete resection is a safe and effective approach that enables both definitive diagnosis and curative treatment, with favorable short-term outcomes.

title: Clinical criteria for suspected early hip osteoarthritis at the earliest radiographic stage: an international Technical Expert Panel study
abstract: Abstract Background Early hip osteoarthritis (EHOA) remains challenging to recognise at presentation, particularly when symptoms are recent and radiographic abnormalities are absent or minimal. Standardised clinical criteria for this stage are limited. This study aimed to develop expert-derived criteria for identifying suspected EHOA at the earliest radiographic stage and to propose monitoring suggestions. Methods An international, multidisciplinary Technical Expert Panel study was conducted, supported by a structured literature review and expert panel voting. Candidate items were generated from the literature review and face-to-face expert discussion, then organised into domains and subdomains. Items were included in the final framework when they achieved > 66% agreement. The perceived strength of each retained item was rated on a 0–10 numerical scale. Results The final framework included two overarching areas: criteria for identifying suspected EHOA and suggestions for careful monitoring. Five domains were retained for identification: exclusion/applicability criteria, symptoms and signs, risk factors, time framework and imaging. Key clinical indicators included load-related mechanical pain, pain during hip rotation, brief start-up or morning stiffness, walking limitation and difficulty with squatting, getting in or out of a car, and putting on socks. Baseline radiography was emphasised to exclude established OA, while MRI and ultrasound were considered selective complementary tools. Conclusions This Technical Expert Panel proposes a clinical framework for identifying suspected EHOA at the earliest radiographic stage and guiding careful monitoring. Prospective studies are required to validate its diagnostic and prognostic performance before clinical implementation as formal criteria.

title: Sliding Amyand's hernia with acute appendicitis presenting as an incarcerated inguinoscrotal hernia: a case report
abstract: Abstract Background : Amyand's hernia, defined as the presence of the vermiform appendix within an inguinal hernia sac, is uncommon. Acute appendicitis within an Amyand's hernia is rarer, and a sliding variant in which the caecum contributes to the hernia sac adds further operative complexity. We report a case of sliding Amyand's hernia with acute appendicitis presenting as an incarcerated inguinoscrotal hernia. Case presentation: A 56-year-old man with type 2 diabetes mellitus presented with a one-day history of a painful, irreducible right inguinoscrotal swelling on a background of a three-year hernia. He was constipated but continued to pass flatus and had no fever or urinary symptoms. Examination showed a tender irreducible right inguinoscrotal hernia with a soft, non-tender abdomen and no peritonism. The white cell count was 19 × 10⁹/L and C-reactive protein was 142 mg/L. Plain abdominal radiography showed dilated small bowel loops. Computed tomography was difficult to arrange on an emergency basis. Although ultrasonography was available, it was not requested because the clinical diagnosis of an incarcerated inguinal hernia was sufficiently compelling to warrant operative management, and the anticipated findings were unlikely to alter the decision to proceed with surgery. At exploration, the caecum was found to form part of the wall of the hernia sac within the right hemiscrotum, with a grossly inflamed appendix and inflammatory fluid. There was no features of bowel ischaemia or gangrene. Appendicectomy and primary non-mesh tissue repair were performed. Histology confirmed acute appendicitis. The postoperative course was uncomplicated, and the patient was well at three-week follow-up. Conclusion: Sliding Amyand's hernia with acute appendicitis should be considered as a differential diagnosis in patients presenting with an incarcerated inguinoscrotal hernia and disproportionate inflammatory markers. Although the diagnosis is often established intraoperatively, awareness of this possibility may improve operative preparedness. Intraoperative assessment of appendiceal inflammation, contamination and the sliding caecal anatomy should guide appendiceal management and the choice of hernia repair. In this patient, appendicectomy with primary tissue repair was followed by an uncomplicated early recovery.

title: VIT-DRN-OCAFF: An Optimized Cross-Attention Feature Fusion Framework for Multi- Class COVID-19 and Pulmonary Disease Diagnosis Using Thoracic CT Images
abstract: Abstract Early and accurate pulmonary disease diagnosis remains a major challenge due to the rising prevalence of respiratory infections and chronic lung disorders. The COVID-19 pandemic further emphasized the need for intelligent diagnostic frameworks capable of rapidly identifying pulmonary abnormalities from thoracic Computed Tomography (CT) images. This study proposes a novel Vision Transformer–Dilated Residual Network with Optimized Cross-Attention Feature Fusion (ViT-DRN-OCAFF) framework for multi-class pulmonary disease classification. The proposed architecture combines the global contextual learning capability of Vision Transformers with the lesion-sensitive feature extraction of Dilated Residual Networks, while the Optimized Cross-Attention Feature Fusion (OCAFF) mechanism adaptively refines and integrates complementary pulmonary representations. A comprehensive dataset containing 24,860 thoracic CT images collected from public repositories and collaborating clinical centers was utilized, comprising COVID-19, viral pneumonia, bacterial pneumonia, and non-viral lung abnormalities. Advanced preprocessing techniques, including lung segmentation, adaptive contrast enhancement, lesion-aware normalization, volumetric augmentation, and image refinement, were employed to improve diagnostic feature quality. The Vision Transformer branch captured long-range contextual pulmonary dependencies, whereas the Dilated Residual Network extracted fine-grained pathological features associated with pulmonary lesions. Subsequently, the OCAFF module dynamically prioritized discriminative pulmonary characteristics and minimized redundant activations for improved classification reliability. Experimental evaluation using a 70:15:15 training-validation-testing protocol demonstrated superior performance with 99.42% accuracy, 99.31% precision, 99.27% sensitivity, 99.48% specificity, and 99.29% F1-score, outperforming existing pulmonary disease classification techniques.

title: Profound Depletion of CPB2 and MASP2 Predicts Hepatic Synthetic Collapse and Transplant Indications in HBV-Related Acute Liver Failure
abstract: Abstract Purpose Hepatitis B virus-related acute liver failure (HBV-ALF) is a highly lethal syndrome lacking precise early biomarkers to guide the timing of liver transplantation (LT). Aims We aimed to identify core drivers of hepatic synthetic collapse and explore novel prognostic biomarkers and targeted therapeutic strategies for HBV-ALF. Methods An integrated machine learning framework (LASSO, SVM-RFE) was applied to multi-cohort transcriptomic datasets to identify crucial diagnostic hub genes. Findings were rigorously validated in a real-world clinical cohort of HBV-ALF patients using serum biochemistry and spatial histopathology (H&E and IHC staining). Results We identified a profound disruption of the complement-coagulation crosstalk as a hallmark of HBV-ALF. Three critical hub genes—C8B, CPB2, and MASP2—were significantly downregulated. In clinical validation, CPB2 levels plummeted to approximately 26% of the normal baseline, strongly correlating with declining prothrombin time activity (PTA) and surging MELD scores. Spatial histopathology revealed a paradoxical microenvironment: massive necrosis with a near-complete loss of these locally synthesized proteins, accompanied by intense overactivation of the terminal complement complex (C5b-9) strictly bordering the surviving parenchyma. Conclusions The precipitous depletion of C8B, CPB2, and MASP2 serves as a highly sensitive real-time biomarker for irreversible hepatic synthetic exhaustion, offering a novel metric to refine LT indications. Furthermore, targeting the localized C5b-9 overactivation presents a promising therapeutic strategy to halt the necrotic cascade and serve as a "bridge to transplant" in HBV-ALF.

title: Salvage computed tomography-guided brachytherapy for patients with postoperative vaginal recurrence of endometrial cancer
abstract: Abstract Background This study retrospectively analyzed the treatment outcomes of computed tomography (CT)-guided brachytherapy (BT) for vaginal recurrence after endometrial cancer surgery. Methods Patients with vaginal recurrence after endometrial cancer surgery who underwent CT-guided BT between were retrospectively analyzed. The primary endpoint was local control (LC). Secondary endpoints included regional recurrence-free survival (RRFS), distant metastasis-free survival (DMFS), disease-free survival (DFS), overall survival (OS), and late toxicities. Results 50 patients were included. External beam radiotherapy (EBRT) with a median total dose of 50 Gy was administered to 30 patients. The median number of BT fractions was five for patients with superficial recurrence and three for those with visible recurrence, respectively. The median total dose delivered to the high-risk clinical target volume (HR-CTV) (equivalent dose in 2 Gy fractions; EQD2) was 70.5 Gy. The median follow-up period was 44.8 months. The 3-year LC, RRFS, DMFS, DFS, and OS rates were 85.6%, 82.9%, 65.1%, 46.0%, and 87.1%, respectively. In the univariate analysis, HR-CTV D90 was a significant prognostic factor for LC (p = 0.009). The 3-year LC rate was significantly higher in patients with HR-CTV D90 ≥ 67.3 Gy than in those with < 67.3 Gy (100% vs. 64.2%). In the multivariate analysis, tumor visibility and postoperative risk classification were significant prognostic factors for DMFS (p < 0.011 and p = 0.033, respectively). Conclusions CT-guided BT provides favorable local control in patients with vaginal recurrence after endometrial cancer surgery. However, distant metastases remain a major site of failure. Clinical trial number Not applicable.

title: Cerebral metabolic alterations and network disruption in pulmonary fibrosis assessed with [18F] FDG PET/CT
abstract: Abstract Background Emerging evidence highlights the roles of lung-brain axis in the systemic effects of chronic pulmonary disease, but cerebral metabolic and network manifestations in pulmonary fibrosis (PF) remain poorly characterized. The relationship between cerebral metabolism and clinical outcomes in PF was therefore investigated. Results Compared with healthy controls, patients with PF exhibited hypometabolism in frontal, temporal, insular, cingulate, and caudate regions (all P < 0.05). Significant disruption was identified within the parasympathetic-associated subnetwork ( P < 0.001), whereas no significant alteration was detected in the sympathetic-associated subnetwork ( P = 0.1582). Cerebral metabolism was modestly associated with pulmonary function and systemic inflammatory markers (| r | = 0.213–0.373, P < 0.05). After adjustment for age, sex, forced vital capacity (FVC), and diffusing capacity of the lung for carbon monoxide (DLCO), hypometabolism in selected autonomic and association regions remained associated with poorer EFS (HR = 0.426–0.632, P ≤ 0.048). Conclusions PF was associated with widespread cerebral hypometabolism and metabolic network disruption, particularly within the parasympathetic-associated network. Cerebral metabolic alterations may provide prognostic information beyond conventional pulmonary function measures.

title: Wernicke Encephalopathy Induced by Acute Cholecystitis A Case Report
abstract: Abstract Introduction: Wernicke’s encephalopathy (WE) is an acute central nervous system disorder caused by thiamine deficiency, characterized by a classic triad of ophthalmoplegia, ataxia, and altered mental status. Chronic alcohol use is the most common etiology of WE, but the disease is often misdiagnosed clinically as only a minority of patients exhibit the typical symptoms clearly. Case Report: A patient with acute cholecystitis complicated by WE is reported, who presented with altered consciousness and dysarthria. Magnetic resonance imaging of the brain revealed high signal intensity on fluid-attenuated inversion recovery (FLAIR) sequences, affecting the dorsolateral brainstem, periaqueductal gray, bilateral thalami, and bilateral parietal lobes. Prior to the onset of neurological symptoms, the patient experienced abdominal pain and loss of appetite due to acute cholecystitis. Suspecting WE, high-dose thiamine treatment was initiated along with rehabilitative functional training. The clinical condition improved rapidly within two weeks. Conclusion In cases of acute cholecystitis accompanied by loss of appetite and fasting, endogenous thiamine reserves can be rapidly depleted. Early adequate parenteral vitamin B1 administration is critical. Additionally, early and tailored rehabilitative interventions for patients exhibiting significant cognitive and muscular impairments are essential for improving prognosis.

title: Abrupt Onset of Crescentic IgA Nephropathy Superimposed on Glycogen Storage Disease Type Ia: A 15-Year Longitudinal Pediatric Case Report
abstract: Abstract Background Renal involvement is a primary determinant of long-term morbidity in glycogen storage disease type Ia (GSD-Ia). It classically presents as non-immune-mediated metabolic nephropathy that slowly advances from asymptomatic glomerular hyperfiltration to focal segmental glomerulosclerosis. The concurrence of an immune-complex glomerulopathy is exceptionally rare. We report the first pediatric case of GSD-Ia complicated by biopsy-proven crescentic IgA nephropathy followed longitudinally over 15 years, shedding light on the diagnostic vigilance and therapeutic adaptations required for superimposed glomerulonephritis. Case presentation: A 15-year-old male with genetically confirmed GSD-Ia had a history of early glomerular hyperfiltration, recurrent nephrolithiasis, and low-grade proteinuria since age 4, remaining clinically stable for over six years on dietary management and angiotensin-converting enzyme inhibitors. At 11 years of age, despite well-controlled metabolic parameters, he abruptly developed nephrotic-range proteinuria (urinary protein-to-creatinine ratio: 7207.5 mg/g Cr; 24-hour urine protein: 4483.8 mg) and hematuria. Given this sharp deviation from typical metabolic nephropathy, a percutaneous renal biopsy was performed. Histopathology revealed chronic tubulointerstitial injury superimposed with crescentic IgA nephropathy featuring cellular and fibrocellular crescents in 7 of 25 glomeruli, strong mesangial IgA deposition, and confluent electron-dense deposits. Induction therapy with oral glucocorticoids and mycophenolate mofetil markedly reduced proteinuria. Due to residual proteinuria, treatment was transitioned to low-dose glucocorticoids combined with tacrolimus, which successfully achieved clinical remission. All immunosuppressants were discontinued by early 2026. At the 15-year follow-up, the patient maintained durable clinical remission with preserved renal function (serum creatinine: 31 µmol/L; urinary protein-to-creatinine ratio: 1051.3 mg/g Cr). Conclusions In patients with GSD-Ia, an abrupt onset of nephrotic-range proteinuria strongly warrants suspicion of superimposed glomerulonephritis rather than intrinsic metabolic nephropathy alone. Prompt renal biopsy is essential to establish an accurate diagnosis. Combining tight metabolic control with targeted calcineurin inhibitor-based immunosuppressive therapy represents an effective dual-track strategy to induce remission and preserve long-term renal function in this complex scenario.

title: Translating Imaging-based Brain Age Models for Predicting Accelerated Brain Ageing in African Populations: A Pilot Study on a Nigerian Cohort.
abstract: Abstract Background: Brain age is an emerging imaging biomarker for early detection of neurodegenerative disorders, based on the estimation of the brain’s biological age. Existing predictive models are predominantly trained on Global North (GN) neuroimaging data, limiting their sensitivity when applied to underrepresented populations due to geographic, imaging scanner, and biological heterogeneity. We investigated this bias by adapting the standard Gaussian Process Regression (GPR) method to a population-specific (PS) brain age model. Methods: Using a multi-institutional T1-weighted brain MRI dataset from 309 Nigerian adults, we implemented a robust low-compute image analysis pipeline which includes repurposing clinical scans and high-resolution cortical parcellation with multi-stage quality control. The PS-GPR model was trained on regional brain volumetric features from the Nigerian MRI scans and its performance compared to four common GN pre-trained models. Results: The proposed PS-GPR model showed a significantly lower prediction error (mean absolute error = 9.82 years) without age-bias correction and few seconds inference time compared to GN-trained machine learning models (mean absolute error = 10.00 – 16.70 years). SPARROW, a generalizable deep learning framework achieved an MAE of 7.87 but failed on 6% of the test set. This early work demonstrates the importance of representative data to build resource-efficient clinically viable models. Conclusion: This population-specific model is a step towards sensitive low-compute African brain age models. With the expansion of imaging data beyond Nigeria through the Africa Neuroimaging Archive (AfNiA), we will further develop the PS model to identify individuals with accelerated brain ageing for early intervention in at-risk adults.

title: Giant supraclavicular schwannoma involving the cervical nerve root: surgical management and perioperative neurological monitoring—a case report
abstract: Abstract Objective To describe the clinical features, surgical management, and postoperative neurological outcomes of a giant right supraclavicular schwannoma extending toward the cervical intervertebral foramen. Particular attention was paid to the tumor’s close relationship with the surrounding neurovascular structures. Methods We retrospectively reviewed the clinical data, imaging findings, surgical procedures, pathological findings, postoperative course, and follow-up of a patient with a giant right supraclavicular schwannoma. The surgical and perioperative management was evaluated with regard to the tumor’s relationship to adjacent neurovascular structures, intraoperative blood loss, postoperative neurological function, wound and drainage status, and recovery. The case was reported in accordance with the CARE guidelines[1]. Results A 47-year-old woman was admitted after an incidentally detected neck mass had persisted for more than 1 month. Imaging revealed a mixed-density mass with abnormal signal in the right supraclavicular region, measuring approximately 58 mm at its largest diameter. The lesion extended toward the right intervertebral foramen, with prominent vessels surrounding the mass. Preoperative biopsy showed a spindle cell tumor consistent with schwannoma. Immunohistochemistry was positive for S-100 and SOX10, with a Ki-67 index of approximately 3%[11]. Postoperative management included cervical compression with a salt bag, monitoring of the wound and drainage, and serial neurological assessments. No postoperative wound bleeding or cervical hematoma developed. Perioperative management should be tailored to the tumor anatomy and intraoperative findings rather than based solely on routine risk scores[5][6][7][8][9][10].

title: Development and Internal Validation of a CBCT-Integrated Prognostic Nomogram for Tooth Survival in Periodontal-Endodontic Combined Lesions: A 5-Year Retrospective Cohort Study Running title: CBCT-integrated nomogram for tooth survival in perio-endo lesions
abstract: Abstract Aim To identify clinical, CBCT-based radiographic, and patient-level predictors of 5-year tooth survival in periodontal-endodontic (perio-endo) combined lesions and develop an internally validated prognostic nomogram. Methods This retrospective cohort included 288 teeth from 288 patients with perio-endo combined lesions and ≥ 5 years of follow-up. Time to extraction was analysed using Kaplan–Meier estimation and multivariable Cox regression, with backward elimination from 14 candidate predictors. A points-based nomogram was developed from the final model. Discrimination was assessed using Harrell's C-index with 500 bootstrap resamples, and calibration compared predicted and observed 5-year survival across risk quintiles. Results Seventy-nine teeth (27.4%) were extracted, with a median time to extraction of 30 months. Overall 5-year survival was 72.6% (95% CI, 67.4–77.7%). Survival differed by lesion class, mobility, and furcation involvement. Independent predictors of extraction were inadequate root canal obturation (HR 2.41), greater mobility (HR 1.64 per grade), furcation involvement (HR 1.45 per grade), probing depth (HR 1.30/mm), CBCT volumetric bone loss (HR 1.0054/mm³), diabetes mellitus (HR 1.87), and poorer oral hygiene (HR 1.02/%). The nomogram showed good discrimination (apparent C-index 0.812; bootstrap-corrected 0.802) and close agreement between predicted and observed 5-year survival. Conclusion A CBCT-integrated nomogram combining seven clinical, radiographic, and patient-level variables provided accurate individualised prediction of 5-year tooth survival in perio-endo combined lesions. External validation is required before routine clinical implementation.

title: Computed Tomography–Based Assessment of the Congruency of Precontoured Anatomical Clavicle Plates in the Indian Population: A Hospital-Based Observational Study
abstract: Abstract Purpose Precontoured anatomical clavicle plates are designed predominantly from Western morphometric data, and ethnic variation in clavicular anatomy may compromise plate-to-bone congruency in Indian patients. This study evaluated the congruency of a precontoured anatomical clavicle plate in an Indian population using computed tomography (CT)-based mathematical modelling and the Clavicle Congruence Score (CCS). Methods In this hospital-based observational study conducted at a tertiary care hospital in South India between May 2024 and October 2025, adult patients undergoing CT of the thorax or neck were included after applying predefined eligibility criteria. Three-dimensional reconstructions were used to derive clavicular morphometric parameters, and a commercially available anatomical clavicle plate was virtually superimposed on each reconstruction to measure vertical plate-to-bone gap and anterior and posterior overhang. Plate fit was graded by the CCS as anatomical, good or poor. Results Twenty-two clavicles from 22 participants (mean age 44.6 ± 16.3 years; 63.6% male) were analysed. Mean clavicular length was 143.6 ± 10.8 mm. Mean vertical plate-to-bone gap was 2.4 ± 1.6 mm, with mean anterior and posterior overhang of 1.8 ± 1.4 mm and 2.0 ± 1.5 mm, respectively. CCS grading showed anatomical fit in 27.3%, good fit in 45.4% and poor fit in 27.3% of clavicles. Conclusion Considerable morphological variability was observed, and the evaluated plate did not achieve anatomical fit in a substantial proportion of Indian clavicles, supporting preoperative anatomical assessment and population-specific implant design. Level of Evidence: Level IV, observational study.

title: Superior mesenteric artery syndrome associated with recurrent aspiration and difficult ventilator liberation in a post-trauma patient: a case report
abstract: Abstract Background: Superior mesenteric artery syndrome (SMAS) is an uncommon cause of proximal intestinal obstruction caused by compression of the third portion of the duodenum between the superior mesenteric artery and the aorta. Recurrent vomiting can result in aspiration and respiratory deterioration. We report SMAS as a potentially reversible gastrointestinal contributor to recurrent aspiration and repeated difficulty in ventilator liberation in a critically ill post-trauma patient. Case presentation: A 19-year-old Saudi male with severe traumatic brain injury after a road traffic accident was transferred for prolonged ventilatory care after craniectomy, ventriculoperitoneal shunt placement, right elbow fixation, and tracheostomy. At transfer, his Glasgow Coma Scale score was 7/15; height was 167 cm and weight 70 kg (BMI 25.1 kg/m²). During approximately 12 months of ventilator dependence, five attempts to transition from pressure-regulated volume control (PRVC) to continuous positive airway pressure (CPAP) failed after episodes of vomiting followed by aspiration pneumonia, documented by new chest-radiographic opacity and increased ventilatory requirements. Chest and abdominal radiographs demonstrated marked gastric distension. Contrast-enhanced abdominal CT in November demonstrated compression of the third part of the duodenum at the aortomesenteric region with severe proximal gastroduodenal dilatation. Retrospective review showed a narrowed aortomesenteric angle of approximately 20–25° and a minimum aortomesenteric distance of approximately 7 mm. Approximately one week after diagnosis, a jejunal extension was placed endoscopically through the existing PEG (PEG-J) beyond the obstructed segment. Vomiting ceased, and the patient was liberated from mechanical ventilation within one week. He remained off ventilator support for one year of follow-up, with no recurrence of vomiting. Conclusions: In neurologically impaired or post-trauma patients with persistent vomiting, marked gastric distension, recurrent aspiration, or otherwise unexplained difficulty in ventilator liberation, SMAS should be considered among reversible extrapulmonary contributors. An enlarged stomach on routine chest radiography is nonspecific but may prompt definitive abdominal imaging. In selected patients, post-pyloric feeding through a PEG-J can bypass the obstruction and control vomiting. The temporal association between cessation of vomiting and durable ventilator liberation in this case supports contribution from SMAS but does not establish sole causality.

title: FLNC-related myopathy: a description of 27 patients from 21 unrelated families
abstract: Abstract Myofibrillar myopathies are inherited neuromuscular disorders characterized by protein aggregation and myofibrillar disorganization. FLNC -related myopathy, a subtype of MFM, encompasses a broad clinical spectrum ranging from limb-girdle and distal myopathies to isolated cardiomyopathy. We retrospectively collected a cohort of 27 patients with genetically confirmed FLNC- related myopathy. Mean age at first symptoms and diagnosis was 40 ± 14 and 54 ± 17 years, respectively. Among the 27 patients, 13 (48%) had proximal muscle weakness only, 3 (11%) had distal muscle weakness only, 9 (33%) had both proximal and distal weakness, and 2 (8%) had no limb weakness. Axial weakness was identified in 16 patients (59%), facial weakness in 4 patients (15%), cardiac involvement such as cardiomyopathies (hypertrophic or dilated) in 13 patients (48%), and conduction and rhythm disorders requiring an implantable cardioverter defibrillator in 2 patients. Mean value of forced vital capacity was 85 ± 28% and 3 patients with sleep apnea syndrome required nocturnal CPAP. Muscle magnetic resonance imaging showed fatty replacement mainly in thigh muscles affecting the posterior compartment, pelvic girdle, and paravertebral muscles. Mean creatine kinase value was 502 ± 436 U/L. Muscle biopsy showed muscle fiber size variability, intracytoplasmic protein aggregates, internalized nuclei, rimmed vacuoles and type 1 muscle fiber predominance. FLNC gene analysis identified heterozygous missense and nonsense variants in 22 (81%) and 3 (11%) patients respectively, and a complex deletion insertion variant in 2 patients (7%). This study reports one of the largest multicenter cohorts of FLNC -related myopathy, confirming that the disease most frequently presents as an adult-onset proximal myopathy with frequent cardiac involvement. We also identified a relatively consistent MRI pattern mainly involving the posterior thigh and paravertebral muscles. Despite the predominance of missense FLNC variants, substantial clinical and pathological heterogeneity was observed, with no clear genotype–phenotype correlation.

title: Long-term prognostic value and clinical correlates of brain [¹⁸F]-FDG PET in patients with post-COVID-19 condition and neurocognitive disorders: a prospective cohort study
abstract: Abstract Purpose : Brain [18F]-FDG-PET often reveals cerebral hypometabolism in post-COVID-19 patients experiencing neurocognitive issues, but its prognostic value remains uncertain. We evaluated the long-term utility of [18F]-FDG PET in this population. Materials and Methods: We reviewed the prospective SYNPOCov cohort (NCT05610436), including WHO-defined post-COVID-19 patients with confirmed SARS-CoV-2 who underwent brain PET scans and had ≥1 year of follow-up. Final clinical outcomes were adjudicated as good (no residual disability), partial (improvement but persistent disability), or stable by an expert adjudication committee. PET scans were compared with those of age- and sex-matched pre-pandemic healthy controls (n=39). Regional metabolic values were extracted from significant clusters (voxel-level p < 0.005; cluster-level p < 0.05, FWE-corrected) and associated with demographic and clinical data. Results: Seventy patients were included (48.3±11.9 years; 69% female; 26.4 ± 9.5 months follow-up), of whom 19, 34, and 17 were classified as having good, partial, and stable clinical outcomes respectively. Baseline imaging demonstrated hypometabolism in four clusters: right frontal, parietal and lateral temporal cortex, and cerebellum. Metabolic values in the right frontal and lateral temporal clusters were significantly lower in previously hospitalized patients and with pre-Omicron variants (p=≤0.04 and p=≤0.03 respectively). However, neither baseline regional metabolism nor its longitudinal evolution on follow-up PET scans (n=30) was associated with long-term clinical outcome. Conclusion: Brain [¹⁸F]-FDG PET remains a valuable biomarker of cerebral involvement in post-COVID-19 neurocognitive disorder, revealing metabolic signatures associated with acute disease severity and viral variant. While not predictive of long-term outcome, PET findings improve understanding of factors underlying persistent cerebral dysfunction. Trial registration number and date of registration: NCT05610436; 2022-01-07

title: Striatal tissue iron in depressed and healthy individuals and the effect of buproprion
abstract: Abstract Introduction: Dopaminergic dysfunction in the striatum is thought to play a central role in anhedonia in major depressive disorder (MDD). Normalised T2*-weighted (nT2*w) imaging provides a widely available MRI-derived proxy of striatal tissue iron, an indirect marker of dopaminergic function, but its relationship with reward processing and anhedonia in MDD has not been established. In this secondary analysis, we examined whether striatal nT2*w distinguishes individuals with MDD from healthy controls, is associated with reward learning and clinical symptoms, including anhedonia and depression, and is sensitive to treatment with the dopaminergic antidepressant bupropion Methods Depressed (n = 40) and healthy participants (n = 41) underwent clinical assessment, functional MRI, and a probabilistic instrumental learning task (PILT) at baseline, with follow-up assessments after 2 and 6 weeks. Participants with MDD received open-label bupropion treatment throughout the 6-week study. The primary outcome was MRI-derived striatal tissue iron, quantified using nT2*w signal extracted from resting-state fMRI within the whole striatum, caudate, putamen, and nucleus accumbens. Associations between nT2*w, diagnostic group, reward learning, clinical symptoms, and treatment response were examined. Results At baseline, depressed participants compared to healthy controls showed significantly higher striatal and caudate nT2*w values, indicative of lower tissue iron. The marker demonstrated excellent 2-week test-retest reliability in healthy participants. Striatal nT2*w was not associated with reward learning, anhedonia, or depression severity at baseline, and did not change following 2 weeks of bupropion treatment or predict clinical response after 6 weeks. Across groups, females demonstrated higher nT2*w values (lower tissue iron) than males in the striatum, caudate, and putamen. Discussion Striatal nT2*w represents a promising, robust and widely accessible neuroimaging marker of depression, reliably distinguishing depressed individuals from healthy controls while demonstrating excellent test–retest reliability. Larger longitudinal studies are now needed to establish its clinical utility and determine whether it can detect changes in reward processing and treatment response across the course of illness.

title: Assessment of Atrioventricular and Ventriculoarterial Coupling Indices in Patients with Hypoplastic Left Heart Syndrome Utilizing Cardiac MRI and Invasive Hemodynamics
abstract: Abstract Background Atrioventricular (AV) and ventriculoarterial (VA) coupling indices have demonstrated prognostic value in various cardiac pathologies but have not been studied in hypoplastic left heart syndrome (HLHS). This study assessed known and novel AV and VA coupling indices derived from cardiac MRI (CMR) and invasive hemodynamics for predicting adverse outcomes in HLHS patients with stage II palliation prior to Fontan completion. Methods CMR and catheterization data from 45 HLHS patients with stage II palliation undergoing pre-Fontan evaluation (January 2015–October 2025) were retrospectively analyzed. Known AV coupling indices and two novel indices—RA SV -RV coupling index (RA stroke volume indexed/RV end-diastolic volume indexed) and combined RA-RV-Aorta coupling index—were compared between patients with and without adverse outcomes (composite of death, transplantation, heart failure hospitalization, SGLT2 inhibitor initiation, plastic bronchitis, protein-losing enteropathy). Predictive performance was assessed using Firth logistic regression and ROC analysis. Results Ten patients (22%) experienced adverse outcomes. Known AV coupling indices did not significantly differ between groups (AUC 0.48–0.69). The RV-Aortic coupling index was significantly lower in the adverse outcomes group (0.17 vs. 0.23, p = 0.006; AUC = 0.80). Both novel indices demonstrated superior discrimination: RA SV -RV (0.11 vs. 0.17, p = 0.002; AUC = 0.82) and novel RAsv-RV-Aorta (2.13 vs. 3.90, p = 0.001; AUC = 0.86). Nested models showed that adding each novel index to RV-Aortic coupling significantly improved model fit (p = 0.036 and p = 0.048, respectively). Conclusions Novel coupling indices designed for single ventricle physiology outperformed known AV coupling indices and provided incremental predictive value beyond RV-Aortic coupling alone for adverse outcomes in HLHS patients with stage II palliation.

title: Primary Solitary Fibrous Tumor of the Lacrimal Sac Mimicking Lymphoma: A Case Report
abstract: Abstract Background: Primary solitary fibrous tumor (SFT) of the lacrimal sac is among the rarest presentations of this mesenchymal neoplasm. We report a patient in whom the mass was initially dismissed as chronic dacryocystitis during three months of conservative therapy, and an outside magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) report suggested lymphoma. The diagnosis was ultimately resolved by signal transducer and activator of transcription 6 (STAT6) immunohistochemistry performed on the resected tissue. Case presentation: A 50-year-old Chinese man was referred with a two-year history of a painless, slowly growing right medial canthal mass. After three months of unsuccessful antibiotic and warm-compress therapy for presumed chronic dacryocystitis at another hospital, imaging raised concern for lymphoma. We performed complete excision via an external approach together with bicanalicular intubation. Histology revealed a spindle-cell tumor with alternating cellularity. Diffuse nuclear STAT6 positivity confirmed SFT. At one month, the lacrimal drainage system was patent without evidence of recurrence. Conclusions: Lacrimal sac SFT closely mimics both chronic dacryocystitis clinically and lymphoma radiologically. When antibiotics and warm compresses fail to shrink a medial canthal mass, early biopsy rather than observation is warranted. In our practice, STAT6 staining has become the most reliable way to distinguish SFT from tumors that look identical under the microscope. Complete local excision with concurrent bicanalicular intubation can remove the tumor and restore drainage in a single procedure.
